title: Senior Database Engineer
description:
About the role

We’re looking for a Senior Platform Engineer (IC3 level) to join our Database Platform team. You’ll help build and operate a global platform that’s scalable, reliable, and secure - developing the internal database platform, automation, and tooling that powers hundreds of databases across multiple environments. You’ll work on high-scale systems used by hundreds of engineers, shaping how we run databases globally.

How we work:

We believe in automation, programmatic implementation, and reusable design. You’ll think holistically about the ecosystem, while also delivering real solutions - collaborating across the Platform tribe to make our systems more resilient and developer-friendly. At this, you help set and evolve technical standards, design patterns, and best practices for the platform.

As we scale, we need engineers who can simplify complex infrastructure, build guardrails, and deliver platforms that help product teams move fast - without compromising reliability or security. You proactively identify technical debt and plan remediation work to keep risk within appetite.

You’ll work closely with other Platform and Data teams to ensure best practices are followed and the right abstractions are in place. You provide strong technical input into product and platform roadmaps, explaining why work is prioritised and what impact it delivers.

You’ll be part of a team that empowers hundreds of developers to build reliable services faster, with modern tooling and infrastructure at scale. The systems you design will directly impact the availability, performance, and safety of our customers’ data worldwide. You’ll join a collaborative team that values technical excellence, learning, and continuous improvement.

At this, you are a recognised technical leader, shaping both the platform’s direction and the engineers around you

What will you be working on?:

  • Design, build, and evolve our internal cloud-based database platform.

  • Lead these initiatives end-to-end, optimising for predictable delivery and measurable outcomes.

  • Define the long-term automation strategy, including migrations, upgrades, and failure recovery patterns.

  • Help embed security and compliance controls (encryption, auth, RBAC, network controls) into Yugabyte platform components.

  • Be accountable for the availability, reliability, and security of the systems you own.

  • Collaborate with product teams, SREs and DBAs to apply platform guardrails for services adopting database technologies.

  • Act as the escalation point for your area, leading minor and major incident resolution and post-incident reviews.

  • Mentor and coach other engineers, support onboarding, and actively reduce single points of failure.

  • Participate in on-call rotations and provide senior escalation support when required.

  • Represent the team in cross-tribe or cross-company engineering efforts and guilds.

  • Participate in interviewing and hiring activities, following best practices and helping maintain a high engineering bar.

What do you need?:

Essential

  • Significant Platform Engineering experience, with demonstrated senior ownership of production platform systems at scale.

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS or GCP).

  • Strong Python development skills (or similar).

  • Solid understanding of software engineering principles - writing secure, testable, maintainable code.

  • Proficiency with Cloud APIs and DevOps tooling (Terraform, Ansible, CI/CD, Teleport).

  • Clear communicator who collaborates well across teams.

  • Ability to clearly articulate technical trade-offs, business impact, and customer value.

  • Experience leading or significantly contributing to incident response and post-incident improvement.

Highly sought

  • Practical experience with distributed databases at scale (YugabyteDB preferred, or CockroachDB/TiDB/Cloud Spanner).

  • Deep operational expertise with distributed SQL systems in production.

  • Experience or strong interest in implementing migration patterns (CDC/logical replication, verification and rollback) and automation for provisioning, backups and upgrades.

  • Experience building Database-as-a-Service platforms or internal developer tooling.

We are seeking an accomplished scientific and organizational leader to serve as Head of Molecular Discovery Technologies (MDT) team. This leader will define the strategic direction of a multidisciplinary organization spanning DNA-Encoded Libraries (DEL), protein NMR, mass spectrometry-based affinity screening platform development, mass spectrometry-based structural characterization, and emerging molecular discovery technologies. Together, these capabilities accelerate hit discovery, improve hit quality, and enable small-molecule and peptide discovery programs across therapeutic areas.

The leader will report to the Head of Target Enabling Technologies organization and serve on the extended leadership team of Small Molecule Therapeutics and Platform Technologies. Partnering across functions, the leader will help shape portfolio-level lead discovery strategies and drive the evolution of lead discovery through platform innovation, integrated data strategies, and AI/ML-enabled approaches.

The role requires a strategic and collaborative scientific leader who can translate emerging technologies and data insights into scalable discovery capabilities, stronger portfolio decisions, and measurable pipeline impact, while developing talent and maintaining external scientific visibility.

Strategic Leadership

title: Private Oncology Care Navigator
description:
Role Type: Private Oncology Care Navigation & Patient Support
Location: Primarily Remote / Virtual; occasional in-person support may be considered

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Private Oncology Care Navigator to provide highly personalized support to an individual navigating a breast cancer diagnosis, treatment planning, and related health considerations.

The ideal candidate will have substantial hands-on oncology experience—preferably supporting individuals with breast cancer—and combine strong clinical literacy with exceptional care navigation, organization, patient advocacy, communication, and interpersonal skills.

The Care Navigator will serve as a knowledgeable and highly organized partner who helps the client navigate the healthcare system, prepare for medical appointments, organize and understand information from physicians, coordinate across multiple specialists, track recommendations and follow-up items, and implement physician-approved health and wellness priorities.

This is not a physician role. The Care Navigator will complement, not replace, the client’s medical team and will maintain clear professional boundaries around diagnosis, treatment recommendations, and other medical decisions.

Key Responsibilities

The Care Navigator will help the client and family:

  • Navigate the cancer-care journey, including diagnostic testing, specialist consultations, treatment planning, surgery, systemic therapies, radiation, recovery, follow-up, and survivorship as applicable.
  • Prepare for medical appointments by organizing relevant information and developing concise, prioritized questions for oncologists, surgeons, cardiologists, and other specialists.
  • Follow up after appointments by organizing physician recommendations, identifying unresolved questions, and translating agreed-upon plans into clear next steps.
  • Coordinate information across providers, including oncology, breast surgery, cardiology/cardio-oncology, primary care, nutrition, and other specialists, with appropriate client authorization.
  • Maintain an organized care plan tracking appointments, testing, physician recommendations, medications, pending decisions, questions, and follow-up actions.
  • Support informed decision-making by helping the client understand general medical terminology and treatment pathways and identify questions that should be addressed by the appropriate physician.
  • Facilitate second opinions and additional specialist consultations when requested, including helping organize the records and questions needed for those consultations.
  • Provide patient advocacy, helping ensure that the client’s priorities, concerns, and questions are effectively communicated to the healthcare team.
  • Support execution and accountability around physician-approved priorities involving nutrition, hydration, medication adherence, sleep, appropriate movement, recovery, stress management, and other health behaviors.
  • Provide calm, compassionate support throughout the care journey while recognizing when medical, nutritional, or psychological issues should be referred to the appropriate licensed professional.

Preferred Oncology Experience

Strong preference will be given to candidates with substantial direct experience supporting individuals with breast cancer.

Candidates should be familiar with breast-cancer care and terminology, including:

  • Pathology, tumor grade, and staging
    ER, PR, and HER2 status
  • Breast imaging and lymph-node evaluation
  • Lumpectomy, mastectomy, and sentinel lymph-node procedures
  • Radiation therapy
  • Chemotherapy and other systemic therapies
  • Endocrine therapy
  • Treatment sequencing
  • Second opinions and multidisciplinary cancer care
  • Recovery, surveillance, and survivorship

Experience with invasive lobular carcinoma is a plus.

The successful candidate should be capable of explaining general concepts in understandable language while appropriately referring individualized interpretation, prognosis, and treatment decisions to the client’s physicians.

Complex Care, Nutrition & Overall Health

Experience supporting medically complex oncology patients is strongly preferred. Familiarity with cardio-oncology and coordinating cancer care with cardiologists and other specialists would be particularly valuable.

The Care Navigator should also understand the importance of maintaining adequate nutrition, healthy weight, physical strength, and muscle mass during cancer treatment.

The role may include helping the client implement recommendations established by physicians and/or a registered dietitian related to:

  • Adequate calories and protein
  • Healthy weight maintenance or weight restoration
  • Muscle preservation
  • Hydration
  • Managing barriers to eating
  • Appropriate physical activity
  • Sleep, recovery, and stress management

Individualized medical nutrition therapy should remain under the direction of the appropriate licensed healthcare professionals.

Qualifications & Ideal Background

We are particularly interested in candidates with backgrounds such as:

  • Oncology Registered Nurse (RN)
  • Oncology Nurse Navigator
  • Breast Cancer Nurse Navigator
  • Oncology Nurse Practitioner
  • Certified oncology nurse
  • Oncology Patient/Care Navigator
  • Oncology Social Worker with substantial care-navigation experience
  • Other licensed or credentialed healthcare professionals with significant oncology experience

Additional preference will be given to candidates with:

  • Several years of direct oncology experience
  • Significant breast-cancer experience
  • Experience navigating multidisciplinary cancer care
  • Experience with medically complex patients
  • Familiarity with cardio-oncology
  • Patient-advocacy experience
  • Health-coaching or behavior-change training
  • Cancer-nutrition knowledge

Core Competencies

The strongest candidate will combine:

Oncology expertise + breast-cancer experience + care navigation + patient advocacy + exceptional organization + accountability + excellent communication + emotional intelligence + sound judgment.

The individual should be proactive, compassionate, highly organized, discreet, trustworthy, and comfortable working collaboratively with the client’s physicians and family.

Most importantly, the Care Navigator should know when to help, when to ask questions, and when an issue needs to be referred back to a physician or other licensed healthcare professional.

Scope of Practice

This role is intended to complement—not replace—licensed medical care.

The Care Navigator will not independently diagnose medical conditions, determine prognosis, prescribe treatment, select cancer therapies, recommend starting or stopping prescribed medications, override physician recommendations, or provide individualized interpretations of pathology, imaging, laboratory results, or other diagnostic findings outside the scope of their professional license.

The Care Navigator will not recommend unproven therapies as substitutes for evidence-based cancer treatment or advise the client to delay or discontinue conventional medical care.

When medical judgment is required, the Care Navigator should help identify the issue, formulate the appropriate questions, and obtain guidance from the relevant licensed healthcare provider.

Availability, Confidentiality & Working Relationship

This is intended to be a high-touch, part-time engagement rather than a traditional fixed-hour administrative position.

The engagement may include regular scheduled sessions, preparation before important medical appointments, follow-up after specialist consultations, care-plan organization, tracking outstanding actions and decisions, and reasonable communication between sessions when significant care-navigation needs arise.

Occasional participation in or support surrounding important medical appointments may also be appropriate when requested and authorized.

Because the role may involve access to sensitive personal and medical information, the Care Navigator must demonstrate exceptional discretion and maintain confidentiality in accordance with applicable professional, legal, and contractual obligations.

Specific scheduling, availability, communication expectations, compensation, and scope of engagement will be discussed during the interview process.

title: Director of Aquatics (4872)
location: North Valley Family YMCA - Porter Ranch, CA 91326
description:
POSITION SUMMARY
The Aquatics Director will manage the Aquatics Department, ensure the Aquatics Department is meeting its monthly, quarterly, and annual goals and objectives, and ensure compliance with all Association standards and safety procedures. The Aquatics Director will hire, train, evaluate and supervise staff and volunteers for all Aquatics Program areas, develop and manage the Aquatics Department budget, and provide leadership and support to the annual fundraising campaign and other volunteer committees, as assigned.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Direct and supervise program activities to meet the needs of the community and fulfill YMCA objectives. Establishes new program activities and expands program within the community in accordance with strategic and operating plans. Develops and maintains collaborative relationships with community organizations.
  • Provide direct supervision to department staff on-site and off-site, assuring that all staff are qualified, certified, and are meeting minimum performance standards for their position.
  • Recruit and hire staff using screen tools and panel interviews to gain the best possible fit for each opening.
  • Provide training for staff and volunteers on an on-going basis through staff meetings, special courses and workshops.
  • Maintain current and up-to-date records for all staff that require certifications and keeps copies on file. Ensure that all job descriptions and performance standards are accurate, current and on file for all employees.
  • Develop work schedules, coordinate daily work, and make sure timecards are properly recorded by employees.
  • Monitor daily pool operations to adhere to all state, local and YMCA health and safety regulations.
  • Conducts and ensures proper maintenance of pool(s). Secures and schedules pool facilities. Maintains accurate records of pool chemical levels and facility maintenance.
  • Models relationship building skills in all interactions. Responds to all member and community inquires and complaints in a timely manner.
  • Monitors and evaluates the effectiveness of and participation in Aquatic programs.
  • Develops annual operating budget for aquatic programs. Manage department budget to achieve monthly, quarterly and annual goals.
  • Identify program volunteer positions and assist with the identification, hiring and tracking of program volunteers; Ensure all assigned committees have appropriate staff leadership, commission statements and chart of works.
  • Creates member involvement opportunities on a year round basis to support annual fundraising goals, including year round recruitment and committee involvement; Responsible for recruitment and retention of Community Support Campaign leadership.
  • Maintains commitment to safety through regularly scheduled safety inspections. Meets Association Aquatic standards regarding safety and risk management.
  • Responsible for marketing Aquatic programs to members and the community through events, initiatives and activities for members and the community.
  • Communicate program information, registration information, schedules, etc., effectively and consistently with branch management and membership staff.
  • Ensure swim lessons are being instructed using the YMCA of the USA swim lesson program; create and ensure there is a nurturing environment for swim lesson participants.
  • While on duty as a lifeguard, provides continuous, uninterrupted scanning of pool and aquatic area.
  • Reviews all emergency procedures and responds to emergency situations immediately in accordance with YMCA policies and procedures. Completes related reports as required.
  • Follow and ensure Minimum Standards of Safety for Aquatic Activities 7.301 are being met. Understands and consistently enforces safety rules, policies and guidelines for the pool and aquatic area.
  • Maintains accurate records as required by the YMCA and/or the state Health Department code.
  • Performs equipment checks and ensures appropriate equipment is available as needed.
  • Plays an active role in continuing to identify ways to improve safety standards.
  • Maintains effective, positive relationships with members, participants and other staff.
  • Continuously monitors aquatic area for hazardous or unsafe conditions. Immediately reports all hazardous or unsafe conditions to management and takes appropriate action
  • Uses problem solving skills to make quick decisions, instruct, evaluate, supervise, and recognize the potential for danger or injury.
  • Successfully completes and pass periodic aquatic safety assessments.
  • Sustain and demonstrate the listed physical demands below:
    • Ability to perform the following:
      • Tread water for 2 minutes (legs only)
      • Swim 250 yards of front crawl
      • Swim 50 yards of each:
      • Front crawl with the head up
      • Breaststroke
      • Breaststroke with the head up
      • Elementary backstroke kick with hands on the chest
      • Perform a feet-first surface-dive in 8 to 10 feet of water (if branch facility accommodates). Then swim underwater for 15 feet.
      • Starting in the shallow end of the water, sprint for a distance of approximately 60 feet then perform an arm-over-arm surface dive in 8 to 10 feet (if branch facility accommodates).
      • Pick up an object (dive ring) from the bottom of pool, surface and tread water for at least one minute with legs only, replace the object back to the bottom of the pool where it was found.
      • Swim the remaining length to end of pool, and hoist yourself out of water.
      • Immediately begin CPR on an adult manikin for 2 minutes, stand and listen to directions from instructor.
    • Sit for extended periods of time in an elevated chair.
    • Must remain alert and focused on the entire zone of responsibility for extended periods of time, even under conditions of high heat and humidity, with no lapses in consciousness. Move safely to various locations, including entering and exiting an elevated chair, while scanning the zone of responsibility.
    • Adequate ability to hear noises and distinguish distress signals.
    • Must understand that significant background noise exists in all indoor and outdoor aquatic environments.
    • Ability to continuously scan all areas of the pool with clear vision.
    • Ability to perform strenuous physical tasks necessary for a water rescue Communicate with others immediately when responding to an incident or an emergency. Must be able to communicate verbally, including projecting their voice across distances; communicate swiftly and clearly with emergency personnel over the telephone and or in person; and effectively give and receive directions.
    • Perform all rescue, resuscitation, and survival skills.
    • Act swiftly in an emergency and take action even when unsure whether a person is really in danger.
  • Attend staff meetings and trainings as required.
  • Uphold YMCA policies for safety, supervision, mandated reporting and risk management.
  • Demonstrate the Six Pillars of Character (Trustworthiness, Citizenship, Respect, Responsibility, Caring, Fairness) as well as the YMCA Core Values of caring, respect, honesty and responsibility in all dealings with members, guests, volunteers and fellow staff.
  • Demonstrate competencies in and willingness to develop in the Cause Driven Leadership areas of mission advancement, collaboration, operational effectiveness and personal growth.
  • All other duties as assigned by your supervisor.

YMCA LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES
The Y’s Leadership Competency Model is comprised of 14 Leadership Competencies (leadership knowledge, skills, and behaviors required for success in the Y), organized by the four disciplines of Cause-Driven Leadership:

  • Advancing Our Mission & Cause: Provide visionary leadership to the organization and to ensure that all resources are mobilized to adapt to new challenges and needs in the community
    • Competencies Include: Change Leadership, Engaging Community, Philanthropy, & Volunteerism
  • Building Relationships: Connect people to the Y’s cause by developing inclusive relationships, partnerships and collaborations so that Ys can co-create solutions to pressing social needs
    • Competencies Include: Collaboration, Communication & Influence, & Inclusion
  • Leading Operations: ensure relevance, effectiveness, and sustainability of the organization so that we can continue to fulfill our promise to the community
    • Competencies Include: Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Fiscal Management, Functional Expertise, Innovation, & Program/Project Management
  • Developing & Inspiring Others: support the holistic development of self and others so that everyone can embrace the Y’s cause, sustain the Y’s culture, and inspire others to take individual and collective action to further our impact
    • Competencies Include: Emotional Maturity & Developing Self & Others

While all competencies are significant the following are critical to success in this position:

  • Engaging Community
  • Inclusion
  • Critical Thinking & Decision-Making
  • Emotional Maturity

title: Metrology Specialist
description:

The Metrology Specialist is responsible for the maintenance, calibration, qualification, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management of laboratory instrumentation used in regulated laboratory environments. This role ensures instruments remain compliant, accurate, and operational while supporting quality systems, validation activities, and continuous improvement initiatives. The successful candidate will serve as a technical resource for instrumentation-related activities and collaborate closely with laboratory and quality teams to maintain compliance with GxP requirements.

  • Perform maintenance, calibration, qualification, and validation activities on routine and advanced laboratory instrumentation in accordance with established procedures and regulatory requirements.
  • Maintain laboratory instruments in a validated and compliant state through preventative maintenance, routine testing, troubleshooting, and repair activities.
  • Investigate and resolve instrument-related issues, document findings, and implement corrective actions as necessary.
  • Support the implementation, qualification, and validation of new laboratory instrumentation and systems.
  • Assist in the development and execution of validation protocols, test scripts, and related documentation.

  • Prioritize and complete assigned projects and tasks to meet departmental timelines and business needs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ISO 17025 calibration programs and measurement uncertainty assessments.
  • Experience supporting pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract laboratory environments.
  • Familiarity with computerized laboratory systems and instrument qualification processes.

Basic Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Physical Sciences, Engineering Technology, Instrumentation, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline.
  • Minimum of 8 years of experience in GxP-regulated laboratories, metrology, calibration, instrumentation maintenance, or related technical support functions.
  • Equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience may be considered (e.g., 12+ years of directly related experience).

title: Senior Backend Developer
description:
Join Protein Works as our Senior Backend Developer, and build a greenfield, cloud-native platform from the ground up using Go and modern microservices architecture.

About The Role

The Protein Works is a UK direct-to-consumer sports nutrition brand. We develop and manufacture our own products, sell them through our own e-commerce platform and ship them from our own warehouse. Behind the website sits a set of internal applications connecting orders, stock, finance, fulfilment and manufacturing, alongside a growing number of marketplaces and third‑party services.

We are replacing those legacy internal applications with a new cloud‑native platform: independently deployable services that will become the single integration layer between the website, finance, warehouse and manufacturing, and a foundation for AI‑assisted automation across the business. This role is a core builder of that platform.

You will join a small, polyglot engineering team working DevOps, Information Security, Data and IT. Go is our preferred language for services because of its performance and operational simplicity, but we hire for engineering depth first: if your background is C#, Java or PHP and you are willing to work in Go, we want to hear from you.

What you will do

Platform Development & Architecture: Design, build, and maintain microservices and domain models (orders, stock, fulfilment, finance) using Go, Domain‑Driven Design, enterprise integration patterns, and clean architecture to incrementally replace legacy applications.

Integration & Asynchronous Workflows: Build event‑driven and queue‑based workflows with REST APIs, authentication, idempotency, and contract testing to connect e‑commerce, ERP, WMS, finance, and manufacturing systems.

Operations, Security & AI: Own end‑to‑end delivery including containers, CI/CD, IaC, full observability (metrics, traces, logs), security/privacy compliance (OWASP, GDPR, pen testing), and day‑to‑day use of AI‑assisted/agentic tools.

Cross‑Functional Leadership: Collaborate across tech and business teams, write ADRs, contribute to golden‑path templates/standards, and translate business needs into technical execution.

What you will bring

Essential

  • Backend & Architecture: 5+ years of backend development (Go, Java, C#, or PHP with a focus/openness to Go) with strong CS/software engineering foundations, SOLID principles, and clean/event‑driven patterns across microservices and monoliths.
  • Data & Async Systems: Solid background in relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server) and asynchronous messaging (queues, events, retries, idempotency).
  • DevOps & Observability: Practical experience with Docker, Linux/Windows, Git/GitHub, Jira/Agile, monitoring/alerting, and diagnostic/profiling tools in high‑volume e-commerce environments.
  • Communication & AI Integration: Strong problem‑solving and stakeholder communication skills, coupled with active practice using AI development/coding tools.

Desirable

  • AI & Cloud Technologies: Agentic AI (LLMs, frameworks, guardrails) and cloud platforms (AWS, IaC/Terraform, serverless, managed messaging, Kubernetes, Redis, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch).
  • Advanced Engineering & Integrations: Production Go experience, GoF/Enterprise integration patterns, durable workflows, contract testing, ERP/WMS/e‑commerce integrations, OpenTelemetry/Grafana/Datadog, and OWASP/ISO 27001 security standards.

How we work

Two‑week sprints for planned platform work and a Kanban lane for operational and integration requests, both in Jira. Pull requests with code review, automated tests and CI/CD to staging and production. Architecture Decision Records for anything that changes the shape of the platform, and golden‑path templates per language so services stay consistent without forcing one runtime. Observability, security and documentation are part of the definition of done.

  • Hybrid working
  • A greenfield platform to build, a modern toolchain and direct access to the decisions that shape both
  • Company bonus eligibility
  • Exclusive staff discounts
  • Private healthcare
  • Birthday day off
  • Pension scheme
  • Access to staff discounts
  • Staff socials and events
  • Refreshments on‑site

description:
The role

As a member of the Global Service Delivery team and within the Global Talent Acquisition function, aligned to the Global Talent & Development Centre of Excellence within Global HR, you will deliver talent intelligence activities that provide market insights, competitor intelligence, talent mapping and research to inform talent acquisition and broader talent planning decisions across Clifford Chance.

Working closely with Talent Acquisition colleagues, HR Business Partners and business stakeholders, you will conduct research and analysis to identify talent opportunities, understand market trends and enhance intelligence-led decision making. Through talent mapping, market analysis and competitor insights, you will contribute to a more proactive and informed approach to attracting, engaging and retaining talent aligned to the firm's strategic priorities.

The role takes a longer-term view of talent markets, talent flows, emerging skills and competitor activity, helping the firm build a deeper understanding of the external talent landscape and future talent opportunities.

Who you will work with

You will collaborate closely with Talent Acquisition colleagues, HR Business Partners and business stakeholders, providing market intelligence, talent insights and research that enhances recruitment and talent planning discussions.

You will also work alongside the Client Insights & Business Intelligence team within Business Development & Marketing and colleagues across Global HR, sharing expertise and insight to support wider business objectives.

You will work globally, partnering with colleagues across multiple jurisdictions, practice areas and time zones.

What you will be responsible for

You will be responsible for delivering talent intelligence, market research and talent mapping activities that support talent acquisition and broader workforce planning initiatives across the firm.

Your time will primarily be focused on:

  • Talent intelligence and market research
  • Competitor and talent market monitoring
  • Talent mapping and candidate identification
  • Insight generation and reporting
  • Stakeholder collaboration and advisory input
  • Employer brand and talent market insights
  • Research technology and process enhancement
  • Strategic talent projects

You will provide intelligence and analysis that enhances talent decision making and enables a more informed, data-driven approach to talent acquisition and talent planning.

What you will do

Talent Intelligence & Market Insights

  • Monitor and analyse legal talent markets, competitor firms and industry developments.
  • Track talent movement across key markets, practice areas and competitor organisations.
  • Conduct research into talent availability, emerging skills, workforce trends and market developments.
  • Produce talent intelligence briefings, market updates and insight reports.
  • Identify talent opportunities aligned to strategic hiring priorities.
  • Translate research findings into practical insights and recommendations.
  • Maintain knowledge of key talent markets, competitor activity and emerging trends.

Talent Mapping & Research

  • Deliver talent mapping and research projects across key markets, practice areas and Global Product Groups.
  • Identify relevant talent pools, competitor organisations and external talent populations.
  • Develop talent maps and market intelligence aligned to current and future hiring priorities.
  • Monitor talent movement and market developments across strategically important talent segments.
  • Conduct targeted market research for critical hiring and talent planning initiatives.
  • Maintain visibility of external talent aligned to business growth priorities.
  • Enhance talent pipeline development through research and talent market insight.

Competitive Intelligence

  • Conduct competitor research and market monitoring activities.
  • Track organisational developments, hiring trends and talent movement across competitor firms.
  • Produce competitor intelligence reports and market updates.
  • Identify market trends that may influence talent acquisition strategies.
  • Highlight talent opportunities, market risks and emerging developments.
  • Share competitor insight that enhances understanding of the firm's position within the legal talent market.

Talent Community Intelligence

  • Provide market intelligence and talent mapping insights that enhance talent community and pipeline development activities.
  • Identify and segment relevant external talent populations.
  • Collaborate with Talent Acquisition colleagues to strengthen talent communities within CRM and ATS platforms.
  • Provide visibility of talent movement and emerging opportunities across key markets.
  • Contribute insights that inform talent engagement strategies and pipeline planning.
  • Develop market intelligence that supports proactive engagement with priority talent populations.

Insight Generation & Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Produce talent intelligence reports, dashboards, presentations and market briefings.
  • Deliver insights that inform talent acquisition, workforce planning and talent discussions.
  • Present findings and recommendations to Talent Acquisition and HR stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to understand talent intelligence requirements and provide relevant market insight.
  • Contribute analytical expertise to strategic talent initiatives and projects.
  • Identify talent market developments that may influence future talent attraction and retention activity.

Employer Brand & Talent Market Insights

  • Partner with Employer Brand and Talent Acquisition colleagues to provide insight into target talent populations.
  • Deliver market intelligence that informs talent attraction campaigns and engagement activity.
  • Identify emerging themes, candidate expectations and market trends that shape attraction strategies.
  • Provide insight into competitor positioning and external talent perceptions.
  • Contribute analysis that strengthens market visibility and engagement with priority talent communities.

Technology & Continuous Improvement

  • Utilise talent intelligence platforms, CRM systems, ATS technologies and external data sources to support research and analysis.
  • Apply AI-enabled tools and automation techniques to enhance intelligence gathering and insight generation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve research methodologies, reporting and analytical outputs.
  • Maintain awareness of emerging talent intelligence technologies and market practices.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance the effectiveness and scalability of talent intelligence activities.

Your experience

  • Experience in talent intelligence, executive search research, talent mapping, market intelligence, workforce intelligence or a related discipline.
  • Experience delivering research and analysis to inform recruitment, talent acquisition or workforce planning decisions.
  • Experience producing talent maps, market insights, competitor analysis and research-based recommendations.
  • Experience communicating insights, findings and recommendations to a range of stakeholders.

title: FACILITIES SUPERVISOR
description:
FACILITIES SUPERVISOR

OKALOOSA GAS DISTRICT

POSITION TITLE: Facilities Supervisor

DEPARTMENT: Operations

REPORTS TO: System Planning Superintendent

PAY GRADE: $37.26 PER HOUR/$77,500.80 PER YEAR

FLSA STATUS: EXEMPT


JOB SUMMARY

Plans, directs, and coordinates the maintenance, repair, safety, and appearance of all District facilities, grounds, and related building systems. Supervises facility maintenance staff and contracted service providers, manages the facilities maintenance budget, and ensures District buildings and grounds meet Gold Standard for Customer Service, safety, and regulatory requirements. Serves as the District's primary point of accountability for facility condition, life-safety systems, and capital improvement planning for buildings and grounds.

Incumbents in this position will be held to the District's Gold Standard for Customer Service.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Plans, schedules, and supervises preventative, routine, and corrective maintenance across all District facilities, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and building systems.
  2. Supervises, trains, and evaluates Facility Maintenance Worker(s); assigns daily work, sets priorities, and reviews completed work for quality and safety compliance.
  3. Facilitates usage and rentals of District facility spaces.
  4. Develops and manages the annual facilities maintenance and repair budget; tracks expenditures and recommends capital improvement projects.
  5. Assists with Solicitations, manages, and evaluates outside contractors and vendors (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, landscaping, janitorial, pest control, fire/life-safety) including scope development, quotes, scheduling, and quality assurance.
  6. Ensures monthly inspection and documented compliance of fire extinguishers, AEDs, smoke detectors, and other life-safety equipment across all District buildings.
  7. Develops, implements, and maintains a preventative maintenance program and asset inventory for facility systems and equipment.
  8. Ensures all District facilities and grounds are maintained in a clean, safe, and professional condition consistent with the district’s public-facing image.
  9. Oversees grounds maintenance and irrigation systems, including landscaping, mowing, pest/rodent control in compliance with EPA standards, and repair troubleshooting.
  • Leads or coordinates facility-related capital projects, renovations, and space planning in partnership with the System Planning Superintendent and Operations leadership.
  • Develops procedural manuals, safety protocols, and standard operating procedures for facility maintenance functions.
  • Responds to and coordinates resolution of facility emergencies (HVAC failure, plumbing, storm damage, security/access issues) including after-hours response as needed.
  • Ensures District facilities comply with applicable building codes, fire codes, ADA requirements, and other regulatory standards.
  • Maintains facility-related records, warranties, service contracts, and maintenance logs.
  • Other miscellaneous job-related duties as assigned.

The preceding is intended to describe the general content of and requirements for the performance of this job. It is not to be construed as an exhaustive statement of duties, responsibilities, or requirements. The principal duties and responsibilities enumerated are all essential job functions.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Associate's degree in Facilities Management, Business, Construction Management, or related field, plus four to six years of progressively responsible facilities/building maintenance experience, including two or more years of supervisory experience — or

Bachelor's degree in a related field plus two to four years of facilities maintenance experience, including supervisory experience — or

High school diploma or equivalent plus eight or more years of progressively responsible facilities maintenance experience, including demonstrated supervisory or lead experience, may be considered in lieu of a degree.

ESSENTIAL COMPETENCIES

  1. Strong working knowledge of building systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing) sufficient to evaluate contractor work, troubleshoot problems, and make sound repair-vs-replace decisions.
  2. Demonstrated supervisory skill, including staff scheduling, performance evaluation, coaching, and conflict resolution.
  3. Budget development and cost management experience, including reviewing vendor proposals and invoices.
  4. Knowledge of applicable building, fire, and safety codes, and OSHA workplace safety standards.
  5. Proficiency with personal computers, MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook), and familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS) or work-order software.
  6. Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to prepare reports, procedures, and vendor scopes of work.

TECHNICAL SKILLS REQUIRED

  1. Must possess and maintain a valid Florida driver's license and a driving record satisfactory to the District and its insurers.
  2. Skill in use of a personal computer and peripherals; ability to use accepted District software applications.
  3. Demonstrated safe driving skills; knowledge of applicable safety standards for facilities and construction/maintenance work.
  4. Ability to read and interpret basic building plans, equipment manuals, and vendor proposals/contracts.

OTHER FACTORS

  1. Must be appropriately dressed in a clean and neat District-authorized uniform or business-casual attire during work hours, as applicable to duties.
  2. Physical Effort: Requires occasional bending, stooping, climbing, and moderate lifting; must be capable of accessing all areas of District facilities, including rooftops, mechanical rooms, and elevated areas, to inspect work performed by staff or contractors.
  3. Working Conditions and Hazards: Works both inside and outside; exposed to seasonal weather extremes when inspecting grounds and exterior work. May be required to respond to facility emergencies outside normal business hours.
  4. DRUG TESTING FOR ILLEGAL DRUGS: Employees in this classification will be tested for illegal drugs in accordance with the District's Drug Free Workplace Policy.

BENEFITS

Okaloosa Gas District offers a competitive benefits package, including:

  • BCBS Medical — 100% employer paid for employee, 92% employer paid for family
  • BCBS Dental — 100% employer paid for employee or family
  • BCBS Vision
  • Healthcare Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Life Insurance — 100% employer paid
  • Short Term Disability — 100% employer paid
  • Long Term Disability — 100% employer paid
  • Accidental Death and Dismemberment — 100% employer paid
  • AFLAC supplemental insurance
  • Air Ambulance insurance
  • Pet insurance
  • Vacation Leave — 80 hours per year, accrual based for the first 5 years, increases thereafter
  • Sick Leave — 80 hours per year, accrual based
  • 11 Paid Holidays, including 2 days for Thanksgiving and 2 days for Christmas
  • 401(a) 8% Employer Defined Contribution Retirement (employer paid, does not require employee contributions)
  • 457(b) Employee Deferred Compensation Retirement Plan
  • Gym reimbursement/incentive up to $50 per month
  • Health Fair — 100% employer paid
  • Wellness Program with incentives
  • Safety shoe reimbursement up to $150 per year
  • Uniforms — 100% employer paid
  • Employee Assistance (Counseling) Program
  • Employee Events — Spring Crawfish Boil, Summer Picnic, Thanksgiving Lunch, Annual Banquet/Holiday Party
  • Up to $3,500 annual education reimbursement

  • Intermediate experience in software applications skills that include, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Program oversight experience
  • Resides in North Carolina, specifically Region 1 (which encompasses one of the 18 counties surrounding Asheville, NC)
  • Maternity experience in OB Provider or Clinic Setting
  • Knowledge of one or more of: clinical standards of care, HEDIS, NCQA PCMH, and governing and regulatory agency requirements

*All employees working remotely will be required to adhere to UnitedHealth Group's Telecommuter Policy

Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). No matter where or when you begin a career with us, you'll find a far-reaching choice of benefits and incentives. The salary for this role will range from $72,800 to $130,000 annually based on full-time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable.

title: Specialty Artist - MAC
description:
OVERVIEW

Experience a place of energy, passion, and excitement. A place where the joy of discovery and uncommon artistry blend to create exhilarating buying experiences—for true beauty enthusiasts. At Ulta Beauty, we’re transforming the world one shade, one lash, one cut at a time. Because beauty is powerful.

If you seek greater purpose—a place of vision, mission, and lived values—where voices are heard, contributions valued and recognized and growth opportunities abound, consider Ulta Beauty. Nowhere else are the possibilities quite this beautiful.

GENERAL SUMMARY & SCOPE

The Specialty Artist – MAC is responsible for maximizing sales in the MAC brand (including color cosmetics, skincare, and fragrance) by engaging guests to determine their individual needs, assisting guests in the selection and purchase of merchandise, and maintaining overall store standards, including cleanliness and replenishment. They represent the image, products, and culture of Ulta Beauty and the MAC brand to the Ulta Beauty guest and support the Experience Manager (EM) through a focus on performance (service/retail sales and in-store events), people (guest service and associate culture), and process (operating procedures and compliance standards). This position requires professional caliber makeup artistry skills, exceptional guest service, and the aptitude to learn and communicate product knowledge.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES (*Essential Job Functions)

The Specialty Artist – MAC is a champion of Ulta Beauty’s mission, vision and values, and should demonstrate them skillfully and consistently by performing the following duties and responsibilities of the position (as well as all other projects/duties as assigned):

Performance

  • Meet or exceed MAC brand sales and service goals and contribute to meeting or exceeding the store’s goals related to retail and service sales, guest loyalty (including credit), omni-channel, and retail shrink as set by Ulta Beauty.
  • Build and maintain strong customer relationships by interfacing with existing guest base, maintaining active contact with a growing preferred guest list, and following up on guest inquiries.
  • Ensure that each guest receives exceptional service by greeting and engaging every guest, personalizing service to their needs, offering samples, and recommending complementary products and/or services.
  • Conduct personalized, professional caliber makeup demonstrations, applications, and lessons; skincare analyses; and product demonstrations with guests to MAC and Ulta Beauty brand standards.
  • Study and practice the Skill Certification requirements and complete as many skill sets as appropriate, within the specified time frame as set by Ulta Beauty and MAC brand.
  • Remain informed, participate in, and inform guests about promotions and marketing initiatives within the brand and throughout all categories/departments of the Ulta Beauty store.
  • Book appointments for and support the execution of services and in-store events that deliver an unrivaled guest experience while delivering on sales goals for the MAC brand and the store.
  • Take the initiative to stay informed regarding new and existing industry trends, products, and services during work time, and be knowledgeable about the ingredients and benefits of these trends, products, and services to better serve guests.
  • Maintain prompt, regular attendance.

People

  • Contribute to an inclusive environment that supports teammates, peers, and the internal and external guests served.
  • Share the benefits of the guest loyalty program, including credit and the Ulta Beauty app, with guests on the salesfloor.
  • Maintain and update an active clientele portfolio for MAC brand sales.
  • Serve as an Ulta Beauty and MAC brand ambassador with all store associates, brand partners, and guests by sharing product knowledge, makeup application techniques, information on makeup trends, and MAC consciousness programs and philosophies, including the “Back to MAC” program.
  • Maintain strong relationships with MAC brand partners through participation in required trainings and the execution of in-store events and promotions.
  • Regularly participate in ongoing training, including brand and category education, to enable continuous professional development and drive MAC brand sales performance.
  • Collaborate with managers and associates throughout the store to help grow the business.

Process

  • Be knowledgeable of and ensure adherence to Ulta Beauty’s policies, procedures, and standards.
  • Adhere to the Ulta Beauty and MAC brand dress code, including wearing brand assets as directed.
  • Drive sales by keeping assigned work area replenished, signed, and faced and ensuring testers are available and maintained in compliance with hygiene standards.
  • Maintain outstanding store and MAC operational standards, including participation in MAC recycling program and maintaining cleanliness of the MAC brand area and any additional assigned area, including the salesfloor, restrooms, cashwrap, backroom, and break area.
  • Participate in completing merchandise resets, planograms, marketing displays, physical inventory procedures, and processing shipment using Ulta Beauty and MAC brand provided technology and best practices.
  • Protect company assets by following loss prevention best practices and providing exceptional guest service.
  • Execute other operational tasks as directed.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS

Education

  • High school diploma is preferred
  • Cosmetology or demonstrator license where required by state law

Experience

  • Cosmetics artistry experience preferred

Skills

  • Demonstrates significant competency in sales, products, and service.
  • Ability to build and maintain strong customer relationships
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Ability to positively and proactively handle guest concerns and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong verbal communication and interpersonal skills

SPECIAL POSITION REQUIREMENTS

  • Work a flexible schedule to include days, evenings, weekends, and holidays
  • Attend brand sponsored trainings

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Frequent mobility during shift
  • Frequent standing, bending, reaching, pulling, pushing, and twisting during shift
  • Continuous lifting and/or moving up to 10 lbs. during shift
  • Continuous coordination and manipulation of objects during shift

If an associate has a disability that prevents them from performing an essential function of the job, the Company will engage in the interactive process with the associate to determine whether there is a reasonable accommodation that will enable the associate to perform the essential functions of the job.

title: Kitchen Supervisor
description:
The Opportunity

We are seeking a Kitchen Supervisor to help navigate the day-to-day operation of the hotel cafe’s back of house, supporting the culinary team across breakfast, lunch, and dinner service. This hands-on role oversees kitchen staff, food preparation standards, and cost controls, ensuring every dish that leaves the kitchen reflects the quality and character of our hotel.

The ideal Kitchen Supervisor is a disciplined, detail-oriented leader who knows their way around a kitchen. They bring strong technical skill and a genuine passion for food, coupled with the operational rigor to manage food costs, labor, and inventory without ever compromising on quality or consistency. Equally adept at running the line during a busy dinner rush, training a new cook on knife skills, and reviewing a weekly food cost report, this person moves fluidly between hands-on cooking and kitchen supervision. They lead by example, hold the team accountable to high standards of cleanliness and craftsmanship, and take real pride in the kitchen they run.

Key Responsibilities

● Supervise daily back of house operations across all meal periods, ensuring food is prepared consistently, safely, and to recipe and plating standards

● Support the cafe and hotel leadership team in training, scheduling, and supervising line cooks, prep cooks, dishwashers, and other kitchen staff

● Ensure kitchen staff maintain required Food Handler certifications and comply with all food safety protocols

● Assist with menu development, recipe standardization, and execution of daily and seasonal specials

● Monitor and control food cost, portioning, and waste; assist in tracking actual vs. budgeted food

cost and identifying variances

● Manage receiving, storage, rotation, and inventory of food product; place orders with purveyors

as needed and maintain strong supplier relationships

● Ensure kitchen and storage areas meet health department standards and are compliant for

random inspection

● Oversee proper use, cleaning, and maintenance of kitchen equipment; communicate

maintenance needs to the Maintenance Manager promptly

● Enforce sanitation protocols, HACCP procedures, and consistent food safety practices across

all shifts

● Coordinate with the front of house team to ensure smooth ticket times, accurate orders, and a

seamless guest experience

● Step in as line cook or expo as needed to support service during peak periods or staff

shortages

● Develop and enforce kitchen conduct expectations, uniform standards, and a culture of

respect and accountability

Qualifications

● 3+ years of back of house / culinary experience, preferably in a full-service restaurant or hotel F&B setting, with at least 1 year in a lead or supervisory capacity

● Demonstrated experience working multiple stations and dayparts (breakfast through dinner)

● Strong knife skills and working knowledge of classic culinary techniques

● Solid understanding of food cost controls, portioning, and inventory management

● Experience with kitchen prep systems, recipe costing, and basic reporting

● Food Handler certification required, ServSafe Manager certification preferred, or ability to obtain promptly

● Ability to lead and motivate a small, close-knit kitchen team under pressure

● Flexible availability, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays

● Passion for food, hospitality, and consistent culinary execution

Work Environment

● Active, on-your-feet role in a fast-paced, high-heat kitchen environment

● Frequent use of sharp tools, hot equipment, and exposure to varying temperatures

● Regular lifting, carrying, and standing for extended periods

● Some administrative work (scheduling, ordering, reporting) performed in an office or at a workstation

Compensation & Benefits

Hourly Rate: $28 – $32/hr | Commensurate with Experience

Additional benefits include:

● Eligible to enroll in Medical, dental, and vision insurance with generous company contribution to monthly premium after 60 days of employment

● Eligible to enroll in Voluntary Long-Term, Short-Term Disability Plans, Life Insurance, Accident and Critical Illness Plans, Pet Insurance after 60 days of employment

● 401(k) retirement plan with employer match after 90 days of employment

● Annual Paid time off: 10 vacation days, 4 Personal Days

● California-mandated paid sick leave

● Ash Hotel & F&B discounts

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

Primarily kitchen-based, with a mix of hands-on prep and cooking, some desk work, and meetings across departments. Some evenings or weekends may be needed around key team milestones, events, or employee relations matters. Ability to sit, stand, walk, and lift up to 50 lbs as needed.

description:
Overview

Company Summary

If you are searching for a fulfilling place to develop your career and an opportunity to make a difference in helping others, then keep reading on. Here at AAC, we have a progressive culture; we listen to your ideas, value a work/life balance, invest in education, and we foster trust and respect for all individuals. We are looking for our future leaders, who are not only going to fill the qualifications for this job description, but who are going to exceed expectations. Be a part of a team whose mission is to provide quality, compassionate, and innovative care to adults struggling with addiction and co-occurring mental health disorders. Our purpose and passion are to empower patients, their families, and our communities by helping individuals achieve recovery and optimal wellness of the mind, body, and spirit.

Responsibilities

Job Summary

The Treatment Advocate (TA) will observe client’s daily activities and assist in their recovery. TA will collaborate with the Treatment team and assist with service coordination as needed for patients. American Addiction Centers strives to ensure that all of our patients receive the most comprehensive care to address the issues that may impede their recovery. The TA also operates the company vehicle to transport clients and facility visitors.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for welcoming new patients, assisting with orientation of programming schedule and rules.
  • Conduct patient belongings search when new patients are admitted.
  • Complete safety rounds and security checks.
  • Participate in coordination of patient’s daily schedule including treatment meetings, behavior interventions, and overall general observation of behavior and level of participation.

  • Support and encourage patient participation in group, individual, and family counseling services.
  • Support clinical and nursing services of patients as assigned.
  • Participate in weekly treatment team meeting and program staff meetings.
  • Ensure that all documentation necessary meet contract, licensure, accreditation and standards for services in a timely manner following the AAC’s documentation policy guidelines.

  • Identify situations which may be potentially harmful to patients and report any patient or safety concerns to Clinical Manager and/or CEO.
  • Understand and abide by State Department standards, facility accreditation, AAC’s policy and procedures.
  • Adhere to company code of ethic and maintain professional boundaries with patients at all times.
  • Respectful of patient rights as well as understanding of patients’ unique recovery needs.
  • Communicate with all staff, patients, and families using excellent professional written and verbal skills.
  • Demonstrate dependability and adaptability with patients and staff.
  • Maintains confidentiality of patient and company information.
  • Abide by the standards of HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 guidelines.
  • Assists in monitoring and managing patient community as a therapeutic milieu.
  • Intervenes in crisis situations to deescalates and resolves crises.
  • Complies with local traffic regulations and reports delays or accidents.
  • Load or unloads baggage or express checked by passengers in baggage compartment.
  • Performs miscellaneous errands such as store runs for patients, mail to and from post office.
  • Makes overnight drives and extended trips requiring irregular hours.
  • Keep vehicle clean, polished, and in operating condition.
  • During all transports, meets and greets all clients in a professional and polite demeanor. Makes new clients feel welcomed and comfortable during trip. Assist passengers to enter and leave car.
  • Answers any questions that new clients may have during transport to help orientate them before arriving at facility.
  • Other task as assigned by direct supervisor within scope of practice.

Qualifications

Education/ Experience:

  • High school diploma or GED required from an accredited institution
  • Associates or Bachelor’s Degree preferred in Behavioral Sciences (social sciences, human services, counseling or psychology).
  • Valid Driver’s License required with insurable driving record
  • Working knowledge of vehicle safety and control systems.
  • Minimum of 1 year experience in a behavioral healthcare field preferred.
  • Knowledge of utilizing electronic health record software and documentation preferred.
  • Ability to read, write and interpret written information, type documentation, present information to groups and participate in meetings.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  • Must be able to work overtime, weekends, holidays, and flexible hours.

Physical Requirements

“AAC is committed to principles of equal opportunities for all employees. The Company will provide reasonable accommodations that are necessary to comply with State and Federal disability discrimination laws”

  • Ability to sit, use hands and fingers, talk or hear, and smell continually. Ability to stand, walk and reach frequently. Ability to climb or balance, stoop, kneel, or crouch occasionally.

  • Work environment is indoors and climate controlled. Occasionally exposed to outdoor weather conditions.

description:
University of Colorado Anschutz

Department\: Medicine

Job Title\: DOM Post Award Core Grants & Contract Program Manager

Position #\: 00729862 – Requisition #\: 41221

Job Summary\:

The Department of Medicine (DOM) has an opening for a full-time Post-Award Core Grants and Contracts Program Manager. This position leads the Post-Award Core team, which provides comprehensive post-award support to Department of Medicine Faculty. This role sits within the DOM Research Office and works closely with research leadership, the Office of Grants and Contracts, divisions within the DOM, and research teams to ensure the effective administration and oversight of sponsored projects. Core hours are Monday through Friday, 8 AM - 5 PM.

Under direction from Research leadership, this position provides day-to-day leadership, facilitates communication related to sponsored project administration, and ensures compliance with all federal, state, University, and sponsor regulations. A critical element of the role is to deliver timely and expert service and support to DOM faculty and administrators. The position is responsible for maintaining efficient and consistent grants management processes in a fast-paced, collaborative academic environment.

Key Responsibilities\:

  • Supervision and Leadership

  • Supervise a team of research services professionals (grant administrators) and assign workloads to team members, ensuring that team members have appropriate workloads.

  • Create and maintain standard operating procedures and policies for the Post-Award Core. Ensure accuracy and timeliness of services provided.

  • Serve as the Department’s content expert in post-award grants and contracts management.

Post-Award Grants and Contracts Administration

  • Perform journal entries, PETs, funding distributions, and other financial transactions involved in sponsored projects administration to complete financial tasks and tracking for NIH, VA, DOD, and private foundation grants and contracts.

  • Implement university fiscal policies and procedures, and state, federal, and sponsor policies and standards applicable to business management of projects (personnel, accounting, auditing, etc.). Prepare budgets for federal, state, industry, university, and private sponsors for grants, fellowships, and contracts.

Training and Reporting

  • Responsible for training the team to provide team members with the necessary skills and knowledge to perform their duties effectively and accurately, including all tasks performed by post-award core, such as journal entries, PETs, funding distributions, projections, and other financial transactions involved in sponsored projects administration.

  • Ensure all grant and contract team members stay up to date with the latest grant regulations, with a specific focus on NIH awards. Provide reports for DOM and division leadership as requested in a timely manner.

Work Location\:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule with a minimum of three to four (3-4) days per week, 8 AM – 5 PM, on campus and as needed based on workload, in-person meetings, and CU Anschutz policies.

Why Join Us\:

The Department of Medicine at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus is the largest clinical department in the School of Medicine. With more than 1,000 faculty, 192 residents, and 200 fellows distributed in 14 divisions, our clinical, research, and academic programs attract the best providers, investigators, staff, and students from around the world who are transforming the future of health care. In addition to our exemplary performance, we continue to have strong standings in national rankings in all our academic missions. Our Department Chairperson remains committed to evolving the Department and meeting the ever-changing needs of healthcare and our patients.

Why work for the University?

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation, and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including\:

  • Medical\: Multiple plan options

  • Dental\: Multiple plan options

  • Additional Insurance\: Disability, Life, Vision

  • Retirement 401(a) Plan\: Employer contributes 10% of your gross pay

  • Paid Time Off\: Accruals over the year

  • Vacation Days\: 22/year (maximum accrual 352 hours)

  • Sick Days\: 15/year (unlimited maximum accrual)

  • Holiday Days\: 15/year

  • Tuition Benefit\: Employees have access to this benefit on all CU campuses

  • ECO Pass\: Reduced-rate RTD Bus and light rail service

There are many additional perks & programs with the CU Advantage.

Qualifications\:

Minimum Qualifications\:

  • Bachelor’s degree in public administration, physical sciences, healthcare, finance, accounting, business administration, business, or a directly related field from an accredited institution

  • Five (5) years of experience managing sponsored projects administration, including at least three (3) years of post-award administration.*

  • Three (3) years of experience supervising professional employees.*

*Experience may be obtained simultaneously.

Substitution\: A combination of education and related technical/military/paraprofessional experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree on a year-for-year basis.

Substitution\: An advanced degree (Master's or Doctorate) may be substituted for experience on a year-for-year basis if the degree is in a field of study directly related to the work assignment.

title: Strategic Project Manager, Allergan Aesthetics
description:
THE ROLE

We are seeking a Strategic Project Manager to contribute to our team and lead project management for enterprise, commercial excellence and internal initiatives for the Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. The role is highly cross-functional and facilitates the execution of business priorities and strategies by: developing and managing project plans, developing and tracking key milestones and metrics, strategic alignment of stakeholders, synthesizing key insights, meeting preparation, and contributing to the development of senior leadership presentations.

The ideal candidate will be interested in working in a strategic, fast-paced, and highly collaborative environment. You are inquisitive, a self-starter, and a problem solver that enjoys working on multiple projects. Most importantly, you thrive in situations where ambiguity is present, and you are passionate about business transformation.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

Strategic Project Leadership

  • Translate strategic priorities into integrated project plans, workstreams, milestones, deliverables, resource needs, and success metrics.
  • Coordinate cross-functional stakeholders, clarify ownership and timing, manage sprints, pilots, and ongoing programs, and drive timely resolution of issues and tradeoffs.
  • Identify, assess, and mitigate risks, gaps, bottlenecks, and interdependencies, anticipate tradeoffs, and recommend escalation paths when decisions or support are required.
  • Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, collaborative, and ambiguous environment while balancing strategic perspective with execution detail.

Governance, Insights, and Executive Communication

  • Maintain project trackers, dashboards, decision logs, and governance routines that provide clear visibility to progress, milestones, risks, dependencies, and realized outcomes.
  • Synthesize complex inputs into concise insights, recommendations, reports, and develop executive presentations that support informed decision-making.
  • Prepare and facilitate agendas, calendar coordination, workshops, working sessions, stakeholder meetings, and drive next steps/deliverables; document decisions, actions, owners, and due dates.

Change and Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with core teams and key stakeholders to align priorities, goals, and deliverables with and advance work across business units and cross-functional teams.
  • Champion consistent project-management and improvement tools, technology, routines, and standards across initiatives that support improved customer experiences.
  • Establish feedback loops, monitor implementation results, and sustain improvements through change-management, frontline engagement, and performance review practices.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

Bachelor’s Degree in related field and minimum of 5-8 years of experience in project management, consulting, business operations, or equivalent combination of education and experience

- PMP or similar certification is a plus

- Robust knowledge and practical experience in project management in the healthcare and/or the medical device industry

- Proven ability to plan, execute, and deliver results for complex and cross-functional projects

- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to design, structure, and lead projects

- Effective interpersonal relationship building and influencing skills

- Ability to effectively communicate and partner with key stakeholders

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

- Expertise in developing executive level presentations and materials

- The ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; and other project management methodologies and tools preferred

OUR CORE VALUES

  • Be Humble: You’re smart yet always interested in learning from others.
  • Work Transparently: You always deal in an honest, direct and transparent way.
  • Take Ownership: You embrace responsibility and find joy in having the answers.
  • Learn More: Through blog posts, newsletters, podcasts, video tutorials and meetups you regularly self-educate and improve your skill set.
  • Show Gratitude: You show appreciation and return kindness to those you work with.

title: Shift Leader - 1590 Newmark Ave
description:
Are you ready to lead a team, manage shifts, and develop your leadership skills while working alongside friendly colleagues in a fast-paced environment? Whether you're looking for a rewarding part-time opportunity or the start of a full-time career in the food industry, we want to connect with you! If you're at least 18 years old and have prior restaurant or customer service experience, we’d love to speak with you.

ABOUT US

Weber Enterprises, Inc. is a family-owned Taco Bell franchisee with over 40 locations across Oregon and Washington—and we're still growing! Our success is driven by our commitment to making great food, delivering excellent service, and taking care of our most important ingredient: our people!

JOB SCOPE

The Shift Leader ensures fast service, resolves guest complaints, and maintains quality standards. They manage product preparation, food safety, and costs while overseeing daily operations, including opening and closing duties. The Shift Leader leads by example, fosters teamwork, and communicates effectively to meet customer needs and maintain a positive, efficient environment.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES

Essential job functions include the following. Other functions may be assigned as business conditions change.

Serving the Guest:

  • Maintain speed with service goals and resolve guest complaints quickly, ensuring a positive experience.
  • Make sound business decisions quickly, keeping the guest in mind, and ensuring employees maintain a neat appearance and deliver quality products.
  • Maintain a friendly, courteous attitude with customers and coworkers at all times, while upholding operational standards.
  • Anticipate service bottlenecks, make quick decisions, and take action to resolve issues.
  • Take action to meet customer needs.

Managing the Business:

  • Ensure proper product preparation, portioning, cooking, and sanitation, while managing labor and food costs within acceptable limits.
  • Coordinate opening and closing activities, oversee crew productivity, ensure equipment is clean and functional, and manage safety/security issues.
  • Execute marketing programs, including placement of POP and suggestive selling, while maintaining restaurant cleanliness and food safety standards.
  • Contribute to daily workflow with regular, punctual attendance and a high level of energy to meet customer demands.
  • Learn quickly and adapt to constant changes in a fast-paced environment.

Leading People:

  • Lead by example, adhering to appearance and procedural standards, and participate in goal setting.
  • Provide constructive feedback, resolve performance issues, and encourage teamwork and collaboration.
  • Communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with the team and managers.
  • Communicate viewpoints and concerns to fellow employees and managers in a constructive manner.
  • Exert a high degree of energy and drive to meet customer demands.

title: Maintenance Director
description:
Maintenance Director (Field-Focused Leadership Role)

The Maintenance Director is a hands-on, field-first leader responsible for driving equipment uptime, wash quality, and team capability across a region.

This role is built around:

40% Training & Development

40% Hands-On Maintenance

20% Strategy & Planning

This is not a desk job. You will spend the majority of your time in the field—working on equipment, developing your team, and improving how maintenance gets done.

What You’ll Own

Training & Team Development (40%)

Lead from the field by training techs in real-time on equipment, troubleshooting, and best practices

Build capability across your team—turn average techs into strong performers

Partner with Operations to train site teams on preventative maintenance and basic troubleshooting

Reinforce standards through hands-on coaching, not just meetings

Help develop and improve training programs that actually stick

Hands-On Maintenance & Field Execution (40%)

Work directly on equipment alongside your team—diagnosing and fixing issues in real time

Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and chemical systems

Drive maximum uptime and wash quality across all sites

Identify root causes of recurring issues and implement permanent fixes

Set the standard for urgency, quality, and execution in the field


Strategy & Planning (20%)

Build simple, effective preventative maintenance routines that reduce downtime

Use tools like MaintainX to support execution, tracking, and accountability

Prioritize resources, parts, and labor across your region

Partner with leadership on improvements that drive efficiency and ROI

Continuously look for ways to improve systems, not just fix problems

Operations Partnership

Work closely with General Managers and Operations Leaders to keep sites running at peak performance

Prioritize repairs that directly impact the guest experience

Ensure alignment between maintenance and operations—one team, one wash

Safety & Accountability

Lead safety from the front—proper procedures, PPE, and clean work environments

Identify risks early and take action immediately

Ensure compliance with all company and regulatory standards


What We’re Looking For

Strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting experience (industrial, automotive, or similar)

Proven ability to train and develop others in the field

Comfortable working with your hands, tools, and equipment daily

Experience with conveyors, pumps, motors, hydraulics, or similar systems preferred

High ownership mindset—you take action and solve problems quickly

Able to balance execution, people development, and planning without overcomplicating things


What Success Looks Like

Equipment is running consistently with minimal downtime

Your team is stronger, more capable, and improving week over week

Sites deliver a clean, dry, and shiny car

Requirements: All candidates considered for this position must submit a valid driver's license and successfully pass a company insurance review authorizing them to operate fleet vehicles. Insurance approval is required prior to the start date

Company description: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and Eurofins Scientific 2/2 March 2023 agroscience contract research services. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

description:
