Job Description

As a Module Lead, you will play a key role within the eLIMS-Forensics programme,

Eurofins Forensic Services, operating in UK, Netherlands, France, Germany and Belgium, sits at the core of European criminal justice systems, acting as the trusted scientific partner to police forces and courts, and providing critical evidence that enables fair and accurate outcomes in serious criminal investigations.
For software engineers, this is a rare opportunity to build systems where code directly impacts real-world justice—supporting DNA analysis, Forensic Case Management, and forensic workflows that can identify suspects and strengthen legal decision-making.

The UK forensic ecosystem remains one of the most advanced globally, combining cutting-edge science, strict regulatory standards, and continuous innovation; advances in data science, AI, and trace analysis are actively transforming how evidence is detected, interpreted, and used in investigations.
As part of the acquisition of Qualitype, Eurofins’ internal model already emphasises the integration of software development, quality engineering, and forensic domain expertise, giving engineers direct exposure to highly specialized scientific applications rarely found in traditional tech roles.

A compelling real-world example is the re‑analysis of cold cases using modern DNA techniques—some decades old—which have led to successful convictions years later, demonstrating how advances in forensic technology can fundamentally change investigative outcomes and deliver long-overdue justice.
In short, a role at Eurofins Forensics offers a unique combination of technical challenge, societal impact, and domain depth—where engineers are not just building software, but enabling a system that underpins public safety and the pursuit of truth.

title: Technical Project Manager – Digital Identity
description:
Are you ready to discover the role of a Technical Project Manager in Netcompany?

We are looking for a technically strong Project Manager to support the development and delivery of European digital identity solutions in a complex, regulated environment. The role combines technical project management, digital identity expertise and EU policy experience, requiring someone who can effectively connect technical, policy and business stakeholders.

Please note that once a month travel to Luxembourg is required.

As a Technical Project Manager you will:

  • Lead and coordinate technical projects related to digital identity, ensuring delivery against scope, timelines, quality and governance requirements.
  • Translate business, policy and regulatory requirements into clear technical objectives and project deliverables.
  • Coordinate technical teams, EU stakeholders, external suppliers and other partners throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Contribute to the design, implementation and evolution of digital identity solutions, including identity and access management, trust services and digital/verifiable credentials.
  • Review technical specifications and implementation proposals, challenge design and implementation choices, and assess associated risks and dependencies.
  • Monitor and manage project risks, issues, dependencies and changes, escalating matters with legal, policy, security or cross-border implications when appropriate.
  • Support formal EU governance processes, including project documentation, steering committees, deliverable reviews and acceptance procedures.
  • Communicate complex technical and regulatory topics clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, supporting informed decision-making across different stakeholder groups.

What would make you a fit for the role:

  • University degree in a related field.
  • Minimum 8 years of professional experience in technical project management, digital identity or a closely related technical domain.
  • Hands-on technical experience in digital identity, IAM, PKI, trust services, digital/verifiable credentials or cybersecurity infrastructure. Experience with secure data exchange, e-government or other regulated IT environments is also relevant.
  • Working knowledge of the EU digital identity framework, including eIDAS and the EU Digital Identity Wallet; familiarity with Verifiable Credentials, OpenID4VC/VP, electronic attestations of attributes and trust models is an advantage.
  • Professional experience working with EU or national policy-making and governance processes, including legislation, implementing/delegated acts, expert groups, formal governance or compliance-driven IT projects.
  • Ability to bridge technical and policy perspectives, understanding the regulatory, data protection, security, procurement and cross-border implications of technical decisions.
  • Professional certification in Project Management (e.g. PMP, PRINCE2 or equivalent).
  • Excellent command of English both written and spoken, knowledge of French would be an advantage.

If you are looking forward to be part of a diverse environment, and have the opportunity to work alongside well-experienced professionals, on challenging, large-scale projects that directly impact millions of citizens around the globe, then this is the place to be!

By joining Netcompany, you will be an integral part of a distinguished team of tech enthusiasts working for international projects, primarily within the European Institutions market, with a unique opportunity to shape the future of digital services in an environment that values ideas and fosters growth.

title: HEALTH AND WELLNESS QA/QI COORDINATOR | TEMP
company: Seamen's Society for Children and Families
description:
This is a TEMPORARY POSITION


The Organization:

Founded in 1846 to care for the children and widows of sailors in the Port of New York, Seamen’s Society was one of the first organizations, in the US, to care for abandoned children in family settings, rather than institutions. Today, Seamen’s Society for Children and Families (SSCF) is a comprehensive nonprofit provider of enhanced family foster care services, mental and behavioral health care services, health home care management, prevention/family stabilization services, domestic violence intervention and counseling services, and a childcare program. The agency’s approximately 200 professionals serve over 1,200 children and 800 families in New York City.


Job Summary:

Under the direct supervision of the Quality Assurance/Quality Improvement Manager, the Health and Wellness QA/QI Coordinator is responsible for monitoring program performance for Article 29-I, CFTSS, Health Home Care Management (HHCM), and Bright Beginnings in collaboration with Program Leadership to support continuous quality improvement initiatives. The Health and Wellness QA/QI Coordinator is tasked with data collection and analysis, conducting audits and reviews, developing performance reports, monitoring Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), creating improvement tools, and ensuring compliance with agency procedures, regulatory policies, and HIPAA regulations. The Health and Wellness QA/QI Coordinator will partner with Program Leadership and Staff to assist in the establishment of monitoring strategies to improve departmental efficiency with a shared goal of creating meaningful differences for the children, youth, and families served.


Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

· Demonstrate a strong understanding of Article 29-I, CFTSS, and Health Home Care Management contract expectations and standards for service delivery to promote the coordination and collaboration of the highest quality services delivered to children, youth, and families entrusted to our care.

· Propose methodologies and, upon approval, conduct monthly internal audits of Article 29-I, CFTSS, and Bright Beginnings to assess quality of practice, billing compliance, and adherence to contractual regulations. Complete and submit the quarterly HHCM CCF chart audit and conduct quarterly eligibility audits.

· Using a Continuous Quality Improvement approach, provide recommendations to Program Leadership to resolve potential infractions and/or identified gaps in practice and/or protocols. Assist in the creation of action plans, provide oversight for implementation, and assess impact. In accordance with regulatory standards, ensure reporting and required follow-up are completed in a timely manner. Monitor corrective action/improvement plans through resolution.

· Develop and monitor Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through visual reporting platforms that track performance trends, highlight program strengths, identify opportunities for improvement, and support data-driven decision making.

· Support the coordination of internal and external audits, site visits, program reviews and evaluations conducted by City, State, Federal and all other regulatory bodies. Provides statistical analysis and trend reporting on the results of all audits.

· Assist in the development, modification, and implementation of SSCF policies and procedures that are consistent with current City/State/Federal regulations.

· Provide technical assistance and capacity building. Educate agency staff on the importance of the quality assurance and continuous quality improvement processes.

· Work cross departmentally with Foster Care, Prevention, Safe Passage Domestic Violence, Childcare to ensure continuum of care for the children and families served.

· Collaborate with other QA/QI Team Members to collectively support departmental work and further promote operational excellence.

· Attend internal and external stakeholder meetings, various staff meetings, and training courses.

· Performs other duties/responsibilities as assigned within scope of position.

title: Egov Select - IT Security Architect
description:
De Federale Overheidsdienst Beleid en Ondersteuning (FOD BOSA) speelt binnen de federale administratie een sleutelrol in het uitbouwen van een moderne overheid ten dienste van burgers en ondernemingen.

Opgericht op 1 maart 2017 ondersteunt FOD BOSA de federale regering en overheidsorganisaties in diverse domeinen, waaronder IT, HR, organisatiebeheer, integriteitsbeleid, begroting, boekhouding en overheidsopdrachten.

FOD BOSA draagt actief bij aan een moderne, efficiënte en digitale administratie die burgers en bedrijven optimaal ondersteunt.

De Directie-generaal Vereenvoudiging en Digitalisering (DG Vd) heeft als opdracht de dienstverlening aan burgers en ondernemingen te digitaliseren en te vereenvoudigen, en digitale diensten te ontwikkelen voor de overheid.

Binnen DG Vd is het domein Infrastructure, Operations & Service Support (iOS) verantwoordelijk voor de infrastructuur, operationele ondersteuning en dienstverlening van diverse federale digitale platformen en toepassingen, waaronder eBox, FAS (Federal Authentication Service), Mygov.be, de Federal Service Bus (FSB) en andere kritieke digitale diensten.

Als medewerker maak je deel uit van het Security Team binnen iOS. Je werkt mee aan het beveiligen van essentiële digitale diensten die dagelijks door burgers, ondernemingen en overheidsinstellingen worden gebruikt. Je komt terecht in een uitdagende omgeving waar cybersecurity, innovatie, betrouwbaarheid en maatschappelijke impact centraal staan.

Taakomschrijving

Als IT Architect, zult u een waaier van taken hebben waaronder
  • Een veilige architectuur ontwerpen en voorstellen om de strategie van de organisatie te implementeren.
  • De cyberbeveiligingsarchitectuur van de organisatie ontwikkelen om te voldoen aan de beveiligings- en privacyvereisten.
  • Architectuurdocumentatie en specificaties opstellen.
  • Het ontwerp van de beveiligingsarchitectuur op hoog niveau presenteren aan belanghebbenden.
  • Een veilige omgeving tot stand brengen tijdens de ontwikkelingscyclus van systemen, diensten en producten.
  • De ontwikkeling, integratie en het onderhoud van cyberbeveiligingscomponenten coördineren en ervoor zorgen dat aan de cyberbeveiligingsspecificaties wordt voldaan.
  • De cyberbeveiliging van de architectuur van de organisatie analyseren en evalueren.
  • De beveiliging van oplossingsarchitecturen waarborgen door middel van beveiligingsbeoordelingen en certificering.
  • Samenwerken met andere teams, domeinen en collega's.
  • De impact van cyberbeveiligingsoplossingen op het ontwerp en de prestaties van de architectuur van de organisatie evalueren.
  • De architectuur van de organisatie aanpassen aan opkomende bedreigingen.
  • De geïmplementeerde architectuur beoordelen om een passend beveiligingsniveau te handhaven.
  • Fungeren als derdelijnsondersteuning door technische ondersteuning en begeleiding te bieden aan het SecOps-team.
  • Je bent in het bezit van een bachelor of een Master in IT of gelijkaardig door ervaring
  • Je vertoont tenminste 3 jaar ervaring in een gelijkaardige positie
  • Je vertoont een uitstekende kennis van het Nederlands en een goede kennis van het Frans. Kennis van het Engels is onmisbare voor deze functie

Technische vaardigheden:
Kennis van onderstaande technologieën, met minstens 3 jaar effectieve ervaring in een of meerdere van deze domeinen
  • Python scripting
  • Ansible Playbooks (Infrastructure as Code - IaC)
  • Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL)
  • OpenShift / Kubernetes
  • F5 BIG-IP (ASM)
  • ELK Suite (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana)
  • Entrust HSM (Hardware Security Modules)
  • Ossec
  • Wazuh
  • MISP (Malware Information Sharing Platform)
  • HashiCorp Vault
  • Forensische analyse- en onderzoekstools:
  • WireShark
  • Velociraptor
  • Autopsy

title: Associate Therapist I PRN
description:
Position Summary

Associate Therapists provide individual, family and group therapy sessions for clients in an Intensive Outpatient and Partial Hospitalization mental health facility, under the supervision of fully licensed therapists. Associate Therapists assess the therapeutic needs of clients, develop appropriate treatment plans, and facilitate group, family and individual therapy sessions. Position collaborates with clients, team members, external clinical partners and family members, as appropriate, to coordinate care throughout the treatment process.

Relationships and Contacts

Within the organization: Maintains frequent and close working relationships with clinical, admissions, and leadership team members throughout the organization.

Position Responsibilities

Essential Responsibilities

  1. Facilitates group, individual, and family therapy sessions in accordance with the clinical program schedule.
  2. Completes session notes, contact logs, discharge plans and other reports in compliance with State, accrediting bodies, quality guidelines and payor source guidelines.
    1. Completes all necessary documentation within prescribed format and timelines.
    2. Ensures documentation reflects ongoing assessments of client’s clinical presentation and behaviors.
  3. Facilitates specialized groups as assigned based on education, training, and experience.
  4. Selects appropriate interventions to meet the clinical needs of individual clients.
  5. Maintains therapeutic relationships with clients using praise and other reinforcers to encourage appropriate behaviors and attitudes.
  6. Sets limits and holds boundaries in a kind and firm manner.
  7. Conducts effective verbal crisis intervention and de-escalation involving other team members, as needed.
  8. Collaborates with an interdisciplinary treatment team to coordinate client care from admission through discharge.
  9. Attends clinical, consultation, and operations meetings; serves as a clinical advocate for assigned cases.
  10. Communicates client progress with the referral sources, families, parents and/or guardians, as appropriate.
  11. Addresses clients, visitors, physicians, and co-workers in a welcoming and respectful manner.
  12. Responds to clients and families with empathy and positive professional skills.

Additional Responsibilities

  1. Can be relied upon to be at work as scheduled, proactively notifying supervisor of planned and unplanned time off needs.

title: Head of Strategy Execution and Projects

The department is part of Strategy, Innovation and Transformation and works closely with colleagues across Group Strategy, Portfolio Management, Innovation, Finance, People & Culture, Communications.

Shape the future with us

Imagine a future with Ørsted

**

title: Senior Data Engineer / Data Architect - Databricks & AWS
description:
TECHNICAL LEAD / PRINCIPAL ENGINEER / HANDS-ON ARCHITECT - DATA ENGINEERING (PLATFORM & INFRASTRUCTURE)

Sydney, NSW (on-site) | Full Australian working rights required - we\'re unable to progress candidates without them.

You’ve built a Databricks and AWS data platform from nothing before: medallion architecture, Delta Lake, real pipelines and real tradeoffs, not a diagram someone else handed you. If that’s familiar, keep reading. Sydney-based, Technical Lead through to Hands-on Architect, genuinely hands-on at every level.

SEEK SELLING POINTS

  • You've built a platform from nothing before. This role needs that again.
  • Haven't led a team yet? If you\'re ready to, this is where you start.
  • Join a 500+ strong data and AI practice, backed by tier-one vendor alliances.

ABOUT THE CLIENT

A top-tier global professional services firm delivering large-scale data and AI transformation programs for major enterprise and government clients across Australia. This is deep, complex platform and infrastructure build work, not light analytics or reporting. You get total ownership of the platforms you build, structured investment in advanced technical training, and direct access to the vendors behind the stack, not just a licence and a support ticket.

ABOUT THE TEAM

You’d be joining a data and AI practice of 500+ specialist practitioners nationally, sitting inside tier-one vendor alliances spanning AWS, Databricks, Google Cloud, dbt Labs, Snowflake, Salesforce and Informatica. The programs here run at genuine scale: think large transport-network digital twin builds, national-scale public health rollout automation, and sustainability data initiatives delivered across Australia and the wider region. Career development is coaching-led, with benefits including dedicated wellbeing leave, paid volunteering and market-leading parental leave.

ABOUT THE ROLE

If you’ve built a data platform from the ground up before, you already know the difference between that and being handed one to extend. This is the first kind. You’ll be designing and building end-to-end Databricks Lakehouse platforms including medallion architecture, batch and streaming pipelines, and Delta Lake at the core, backed by AWS (Glue or Redshift), not a single layer someone else designed around you.

How much of that you own depends on where you sit, and leadership experience isn\'t a prerequisite at every level. As a Technical Lead, you might already be leading a team, or you might be ready to step into that for the first time with real support behind you. As a Principal Engineer or Hands-on Architect, you’re setting technical direction and coaching engineers through the complexity yourself. Either way, you own the platform, not a slice of it.

DUTIES

  • Architect end-to-end Databricks Lakehouse platforms, including medallion architecture, on AWS (Glue or Redshift).
  • Design and build batch, streaming and real-time pipelines feeding AI and advanced analytics workloads.
  • Own distributed systems performance: Spark tuning, query optimisation, and cost and cluster right-sizing at scale.
  • Improve CI/CD, infrastructure as code (Terraform) and automated deployment practice across the platform.
  • Technical Lead level: own delivery of your components directly, whether you\'re already leading others or ready to step into that for the first time.
  • Principal Engineer / Hands-on Architect level: set technical direction across the build and coach engineers through the complexity, not just review their output.
  • Get direct access to advanced vendor training and close working relationships with the platform partners behind the stack.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Proven experience building data platforms end to end, infrastructure through to data lake, not one layer in isolation.
  • Deep hands-on Databricks and Delta Lake, including medallion architecture and PySpark or Scala, with AWS (Glue or Redshift at minimum).
  • Advanced SQL and performance tuning across distributed systems, with real Spark and cloud troubleshooting experience.
  • Databricks certifications (Certified Data Engineer / Certified Professional) and AWS certifications highly regarded, not mandatory.
  • Technical Lead level: strong individual delivery on complex builds. Prior leadership experience is valued but not required, clear potential to lead is enough.
  • Principal Engineer / Hands-on Architect level: demonstrated ownership of technical direction and coaching engineers through delivery, not just managing tickets.
  • Comfortable in genuine ambiguity on large, complex programs, not tightly scoped analytics or reporting projects.
  • Full Australian working rights required. We are unable to progress applications without them.

KEY SKILLS

Databricks, Delta Lake, Apache Spark, PySpark, Scala, Medallion Architecture, AWS, Glue, Redshift, Terraform, CI/CD, Data Engineering, Data Architecture, Data Platform, Data Lake, Sydney.

A note from the consultant running this search: I\'ve placed engineers into this practice who came in as builders and ended up leading their own workstreams within a year. The ones who thrive aren\'t chasing a title, they\'re chasing the platform work that\'s actually hard. If your CV reads like tidy dashboards and light reporting, this isn\'t your role. If it reads like you\'ve fought with Spark cluster configs at 11pm and won, let\'s talk.

title: FinCrime Operations Team Lead
description:
As a FinCrime Operations Team Lead you will develop and oversee the daily operations of a team of FinCrime Operations Analysts or Specialists. Your primary purpose is to ensure the effective mitigation of financial crime risks associated with Wise's customers, while maintaining a strong focus on operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and a customer-centric approach. You will foster a high-performing team, drive operational excellence, and act as a subject matter expert in KYC/AML/Fraud/Screening and financial crime prevention. You will be responsible for ensuring your team meets performance targets, maintains or elevates quality standards, and contributes to a culture of continuous improvement within the FinCrime Operations organization.

The FinCrime Operations Team Lead is a dual-focused leader, combining strong people leadership with domain and operational expertise. You will be instrumental in building and refining processes that prioritise customer impact while maintaining focus on the evolving risks within the financial services industry, specific product vulnerabilities, and the requirements set by regulations and partners. This includes supporting the development of compliant and scalable processes and possessing an understanding of financial crime risks associated with our customers, products, and tooling.

  • Team Leadership: You will lead by example, driving a customer-focused mindset across your team and the wider fincrime organization. You are instrumental in fostering a high-performance, results-driven culture defined by strong ownership and accountability. This involves building and nurturing high-performing teams that value knowledge sharing, continuous learning, and adaptability in our change-oriented environment. Fincrime Operations Team Lead demonstrates strong capabilities in timely conflict resolution and fosters open communication and guides effective mediation to ensure a positive working environment. You should be visible and actively engaged in team management. Your focus is on unifying the team behind shared goals (and wider FinCrime/servicing strategies) and driving collective actions.
  • People management: Coach and develop a strong team of FinCrime Operations Analysts or Specialists with varying levels of experience, providing tailored guidance, and taking swift, decisive action to manage performance issues effectively, ensuring sustained excellence and growth. Provide regular, constructive, and actionable feedback to your direct reports. Coach and mentor team members to support their growth, develop their skills, and help them reach their full potential. Design and manage performance or development plans in identified areas. Conduct career map check-ins and make recommendations for demotions, promotions, salary raises, and other role related decisions.
  • Operational management: You will oversee the daily operations of the team, ensuring adherence to relevant regulations and internal policies and processes. Identify and propose opportunities for process and tooling improvements. Collaborate with central functions and other operational teams as needed to increase operational efficiency or to ensure effective cross-team collaboration on joint initiatives. Provide guidance and support on complex, high-risk cases and escalations. Be on top of timely admin related tasks including but not limited to scheduling, training, hiring, interviewing, organising team activities, and others.
  • Performance management: Measure team and individual KPIs and ensure performance targets and quality standards are consistently met while maintaining focus on customer experience and adherence to internal guidelines. Drive high-quality results for both the team and individuals, continuously enhancing overall quality outcomes. Conduct timely quality reviews, ensuring high decision accuracy and effectively communicate the importance of quality assurance. Conduct regular and impactful one on one coaching sessions (usually on a weekly or biweekly basis), provide clear and actionable feedback. Ensure tasks are managed timely and aligned with the team’s goals. Run team meetings to ensure that your team is kept up to date with the latest information, share best practices and enhance overall team spirit. Addresses underperformance promptly through coaching and setting SMART goals, and ensures all interventions are well-documented. Understand and be able to articulate how to move key metrics at team and individual level through efficient performance and task management.
  • Expertise sharing: Be a subject matter expert in financial crime areas with the ability to obtain and maintain sufficient subject matter expertise required to train, develop and coach your team. Maintain a comprehensive understanding of our regulatory obligations, internal policies, domain-specific processes and best practices. Apply a risk-based approach to deterring and preventing money laundering and financial crime. Perform and support deep dives, understand root causes of problematic cases and propose solutions to senior leadership. Assist senior leadership with reviews and developing our processes, task management and in other operational areas as requested to ensure compliant and effective servicing function
  • Issue Management and Escalation : Escalate tooling or processing incidents, high-risk customer issues, control weaknesses, or other material problems to direct leadership in a timely and informative manner, following established protocols.
  • Planning and execution: Be accountable for driving your direct team's performance outcomes, ensuring key performance indicators (KPIs) are consistently met and enhanced. Possess strong knowledge of team processes and tooling, leveraging data to support initiative execution. This involves taking full ownership of your team's results, setting targets for improvement, and providing insights to stakeholders. Set and progress towards goals, adeptly identifying and resolving blockers or issues, whether performance or metric-related, to optimize output and results.
  • Stakeholder management and communication: Collaborate closely with stakeholders ensuring clear communication and coordination of actions. Your initiatives and reports are well documented and you choose the right platforms to communicate to a wider audience in a timely manner. The documentation has a clear scope and includes potential impact in different areas. You can communicate confidently with difficult stakeholders on varied operational or domain related topics. Proactively work on improving cross-team communication and collaboration, acting as the liaison between different layers of the organization and your own team. Employ impactful and inspiring communication skills, unifying individuals behind shared goals, and leverage strong presentation skills to convey vision and progress.
  • Other: Perform additional tasks as assigned by your lead, demonstrating adaptability and a proactive approach. This includes actively participating in meetings, trainings, workshops, and internal events to support broader team and company objectives.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English, with the ability to produce clear, concise, accurate, and professional reports, summaries, and customer communications. Additional languages are a plus.
  • At least 1-2 years of leading small to medium sized teams, preferably in operations.
  • Good understanding of the regulatory framework surrounding KYC/AML/Fraud/Risk and financial crime prevention.
  • You are familiar with money laundering methods and other financial crime trends.
  • You can build and maintain an environment where your team is incentivised to make decisions and apply a risk-based approach to their work. This involves the ability to guide the team on the right course or course-correct swiftly when necessary, ensuring resources and focus are directed towards the most impactful tasks.
  • You are punctual, independent, proactive and willing to get things done.
  • Strong operational management and tactical decision-making skills.
  • Can work with tight deadlines under pressure whilst maintaining high level of quality and competency.
  • You have excellent communication and interpersonal skills, strong organisational skills, great time management, and ability to work in a fast paced and high pressure environment.
  • Ability to multi-task and take responsibility in challenging situations.
  • You are capable of identifying gaps in policies and processes and providing detailed feedback, including examples when possible, through the established communication channels.
  • A strong process-oriented and efficiency-driven mindset.
  • Proven track record of taking individual ownership and responsibilities as well as being a great team-player. Ability to deliver constructive, well-evidenced feedback that drives tangible behavioral change and performance improvement.
  • Ability to analyze and move of team’s metrics

Nice to have:

title: Director, Payloads Systems Integration and Test
description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About this role

As Director of Payload Systems Integration and Test, you will lead and grow a team of multidisciplinary engineers responsible for end-to-end mission success of a diverse portfolio of payloads, such as inertial, RF, and optical sensors and communication systems, as well as various types of pharmaceutical processing payloads. This role combines deep technical authority with team leadership, product definition, and customer delivery
responsibility. You will own the successful execution of multiple concurrent payload missions, delivering flight hardware that operates in orbit, survives hypersonic reentry, and returns to Earth – reliably and at scale.

Your team will serve as the technical bridge between each payload and the Varda vehicle, defining interfaces, planning and executing payload integration and test campaigns, coordinating in-orbit operations, and ensuring safe recovery of payload data and hardware. When payloads require special accommodations or vehicle modifications, your team will work across the vehicle engineering team to scope and implement these changes.

As Director, you will manage day-to-day execution across the team, in addition to hiring and headcount planning, new project scoping, and development of standard workflows and processes. You will also own and evolve the Varda Payload User Guide, defining standard interfaces and accommodations for hosted payloads, and developing a roadmap that expands the set of customers and use cases Varda can support while simultaneously growing mission cadence.

Responsibilities

  • Build and lead the Payload Systems Integration & Test team, hiring and developing engineers across a range of experience levels
  • Own integration and test for Varda's internal pharmaceutical processing payloads: test planning, functional and process verification, contamination control, and environmental qualification of fluidic and thermal flight hardware
  • Partner closely with Payload & Mechanisms development engineers on pharma payload designs, staying engaged early enough in the design cycle to shape testability, and supporting the fast iteration these programs run on
  • Take ambiguous customer mission objectives and determine how to meet them with the existing platform, or scope the non-recurring engineering needed and bring in the right development teams
  • Own payload interface definition and requirements: ICDs, interface verification, and the standards documentation (payload user guide) that external customers and internal teams work from
  • Plan and execute payload integration and test campaigns across both lines, including interface verification, functional testing, and environmental qualification (random vibration, thermal vacuum, EMI/EMC, shock)
  • Work with the production crew building and integrating payload hardware, and establish the cleanroom practices both lines depend on
  • Coordinate with Vehicle Integration & Test as a sister function, sharing practices and infrastructure where it makes sense while maintaining distinct practices where appropriate
  • Work with Mission Management to hit contract milestones and customer commitments, and serve as the technical face to customers through the mission lifecycle
  • Support payload operations through flight, reentry, and recovery
  • Establish and mature the processes, documentation, and cleanroom practices that let payload integration scale with mission cadence

Basic Qualifications

  • 10+ years of spacecraft or aerospace hardware experience spanning integration, test, and mission execution
  • Demonstrated ability to take poorly-defined technical problems and turn them into executable plans, interfaces, and requirements
  • Hands-on experience planning and running environmental qualification campaigns on flight hardware
  • Strong interface engineering background: ICDs, requirements flow-down, interface verification across organizational boundaries
  • Experience leading engineers, including hiring and developing early-career talent
  • Breadth across mechanical, thermal, fluidic, electrical, and software interfaces, with enough depth to be a credible technical backstop for the team
  • Cleanroom operations and contamination control
  • Customer-facing experience: scoping work, managing execution schedules, setting expectations, and negotiating technical commitments
  • B.S. in a relevant engineering discipline

Preferred Qualifications

  • Active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility to be granted one
  • Test and verification experience with fluidic, thermal, or process hardware (pharmaceutical, biological, chemical, or life sciences payloads)
  • Experience with payload accommodation on a hosted or rideshare platform
  • Reentry, recovery, or landed-vehicle experience
  • Defense or government program experience
  • Experience standing up a new function or team
  • M.S. in aerospace, mechanical, chemical, or systems engineering

Pay Range

  • Salary range: $185,640 - $251,160 /per year
  • This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA
  • Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance
  • You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

Benefits

Consider your benefits covered for launch. At Varda, we invest in benefits and perks that support your health, financial well-being, and life beyond work. Benefits vary by position, with packages designed specifically for our regular full-time employees and interns.

Regular Full-Time Positions:

title: Mechanical Spacecraft Technician (I–III)
description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

  • Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.
  • What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.
  • It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

YOUR MISSION

As a Mechanical Spacecraft Technician, you will play a vital role in the assembly, integration, and testing of spacecraft mechanical systems. You will collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to build spacecraft hardware from early development through environmental testing, flight readiness, and production ramp. This role may be leveled from Technician I to Technician III based on experience, skills, and demonstrated proficiency.

RESPONSIBILITIES
Mechanical Assembly: Build, install, and inspect spacecraft mechanical hardware—including primary and secondary structures, panels, brackets, payloads, mechanisms, deployables, thermal hardware, fasteners, and support equipment—using engineering
drawings, work instructions, and process documentation.
Component Preparation and Handling: Prepare, clean, protect, and handle flight and flight-like hardware. Perform precision assembly operations including torqueing, safety wiring, staking, bonding, shimming, alignment, and mechanical fastening while maintaining hardware traceability and configuration control.
Spacecraft Integration: Support the integration of mechanical subsystems and components into spacecraft structures. Install and route hardware, perform fit checks and dimensional inspections, and support closeouts and access panel installation.
Testing and Validation: Support mechanical functional testing, deployment testing, alignment checks, mass properties measurements, vibration testing, acoustic testing, thermal vacuum testing, and other environmental test activities. Set up test hardware and
fixtures, follow approved procedures, and accurately record results.
Inspection and Troubleshooting: Perform visual, dimensional, and workmanship inspections. Identify and document hardware discrepancies, support nonconformance investigations, and work with engineering and quality teams to resolve assembly and integration issues.
Tooling and Ground Support Equipment: Operate and maintain hand tools, torque tools, precision measurement equipment, lifting equipment, assembly fixtures, and mechanical ground-support equipment. Support the development and improvement of tooling and work instructions.
Safety and Compliance: Follow requirements for FOD prevention, ESD control, cleanroom operations, hazardous materials, lifting and handling, contamination control, and safe work around energized and flight hardware.
Continuous Improvement: Provide feedback on assembly processes, drawings, work instructions, tooling, and manufacturing methods to improve safety, quality, repeatability, and schedule performance.

QUALIFICATIONS
• Technical degree, certificate, apprenticeship, or equivalent training in mechanical, aerospace, manufacturing, or a related field.
• Relevant experience in spacecraft, aerospace, defense, automotive, precision manufacturing, or other high-reliability mechanical assembly environments.
• Experience assembling and integrating mechanical structures, mechanisms, brackets, panels, fasteners, or related hardware.
• Proficiency reading engineering drawings, schematics, work instructions, process sheets, and assembly procedures.
• Experience using hand tools, torque tools, precision measurement equipment, and mechanical test equipment.
• Experience with mechanical alignment, dimensional inspection, shimming, bonding, staking, or safety wiring.
• Experience working in ESD-sensitive, FOD-critical, and cleanroom environments.
• Ability to follow detailed procedures and maintain accurate build, inspection, and
test documentation.
• Ability to work autonomously and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to lift 25 pounds and work in and around constrained or confined spaces.

LEVELING GUIDANCE
Technician I: Develops proficiency in spacecraft mechanical assembly, hardware handling, documentation, and inspection while working under regular guidance. Typically has 0–1 years of relevant experience or equivalent technical training.
Technician II: Independently performs a broad range of mechanical assembly, integration, inspection, and test activities. Troubleshoots common issues and supports process improvements and peer training. Typically has 1–3 years of relevant experience.
Technician III: Performs complex mechanical assembly, integration, troubleshooting, and testing with limited supervision. Serves as a technical resource for other technicians and supports development hardware, environmental testing, flight readiness, and production ramp. Typically has 3+ years of relevant experience or equivalent demonstrated proficiency.

PREFERRED SKILLS
• Spacecraft or satellite mechanical assembly and integration
• Experience with primary and secondary spacecraft structures
• Mechanical mechanisms, deployment systems, hinges, latches, or release devices
• Precision alignment and dimensional inspection
• Torque application, safety wiring, staking, shimming, and mechanical fastening
• Structural bonding, potting, or adhesive application
• Experience supporting vibration, acoustic, thermal vacuum, or other environmental testing
• Experience with lifting and handling flight hardware
• Familiarity with GD&T and mechanical inspection practices
• Experience with composite structures, lightweight materials, or additive-manufactured hardware
• Experience using coordinate measuring machines, laser trackers, optical tooling, or other alignment equipment
• Relevant certifications in mechanical assembly, rigging, machining, composites, or cleanroom operations

COMPENSATION

  • Base Salary:
    • Technician I : $26.50-$36/hr
    • Technician II: $31.50-$41.50/hr
    • Technician III: $36-50.50/hr
    • *this position is non-exempt and is eligible for overtime
  • Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Work Location—this a fully onsite position based out of our Centennial, CO office.
  • Work environment—the work environment; temperature, noise level, inside or outside, or other factors that will affect the person's working conditions while performing the job.
  • Physical demands—the physical demands of the job, including bending, sitting, lifting and driving.

This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below. #LI-Onsite

title: Financial Coach
description:
OUR MISSION STATEMENT:

Seeking to put God’s love into action, Indian River Habitat for Humanity develops housing solutions guided by the needs of its family partners and the community.


POSITION SUMMARY:

As an integral part of the Housing Solutions Team, the primary responsibility of the Financial Coach will help households become financially prepared to qualify for homeownership. The Certified Credit Counselor/Financial Coach will provide one on one financial counseling and coaching services to individuals and families seeking to improve their financial well-being. The ideal candidate will assist clients in managing debt, improving credit, creating sustainable budgets, and achieving financial goals such as homeownership, savings, and asset building. The role is vital in promoting long-term financial stability through education, accountability, and personalized guidance.


RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide accurate, relevant, and helpful information to assist individuals in developing solutions for money management, assist in credit-related issues, housing issues, and prepare future homebuyers for lender readiness either on the open market or for Habitat’s Affordable Housing program.
  • Remain educated on all market options for all housing trends (purchase and/or rentals) and refer qualified candidates that have completed the housing counseling program successfully to the appropriately identified market.
  • Conduct in-depth financial assessments to evaluate credit reports, debt load, income, and expenses. Develop action plans tailored to clients’ unique financial situations and track progress over time. Follow up every 30-60 days.
  • Stay connected with emergency housing organizations to be able to assist individuals needing immediate assistance prior to identification of rental and/or purchase options.
  • Provide individualized counseling to help clients understand and improve their credit, manage debt, and establish achievable financial goals
  • Prepare and maintain counseling files. Maintain accurate documentation of counseling sessions, progress notes, and required reporting in compliance with agency standards.
  • Assist families with all applications for housing and make sure that all applications are complete, and all requirements are met prior to application to the Habitat Homebuyer Services Program.
  • Assist families with the application process for other market options and afford them the same assistance to provide a complete packet to a lender or property management.
  • Facilitate HUD first time homebuyer education workshops for Habitat future home buyers.
  • Facilitate workshops and seminars on financial topics, including budgeting, credit building, savings, and debt management for families working with IRHFH.

Location: Phoenix, AZ

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
  • Minimum 6 years’ experience in mechanical design and analysis of aerospace components

WE VALUE

  • Advanced understanding and application of disciplines in high speed machinery for one or more of these areas: Bearings, Gears & splines, Air & oil seals, and Lubrication systems
  • Familiarity with bearing analysis methodologies and software such as ABMA, A.B Jones, ADORE, or Romax

description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SPLUNK ENGINEER

SpaceX is hiring a Splunk Engineer to help protect and drive the SpaceX mission. Our engineers are responsible for deploying, administrating and supporting a distributed Splunk environment at an enterprise scale. As a highly visible and dynamic organization, we must value and guard against damage to our internal information, our physical hardware, and our reputation and brand. It is paramount that we defend against loss of control or confidence in our systems, to guarantee the highest probability of success.

  • Help monitor and maintain the logging platform's performance, availability, and capacity.

  • Troubleshoot Splunk Instances and Splunk Universal Forwarder problems.
  • Data onboarding, governance, enrichment and fields extraction for various use cases.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 2+ years of experience administering or implementing Splunk in a professional setting.
  • Experience writing complex regex for field mappings and identifying patterns.
  • Experience with Puppet, Ansible, or other automation frameworks.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Certifications such as Splunk Enterprise Certified Architect, Splunk Enterprise Security Admin and Splunk Core Consultant.
  • Familiarity with integrating enterprise applications and on-boarding new log sources.
  • Familiarity with aerospace, satellite communications, launch vehicle, or factory-floor logging environments.
  • Knowledge in the Common Information Model (CIM) with a strong understanding between the CIM and knowledge objects.
  • Experience maintaining on-premises deployments of Splunk Core and Splunk Enterprise Security by supporting hundreds of users.
  • Experience in identifying visibility gaps for SOC detections and onboarding custom data sources into Splunk.
  • Experience with System Administration, DevOps, or Site Reliability Engineering.
  • Experience developing or extending Splunk with Python (custom commands, modular inputs, alert actions, or apps) beyond basic SPL.
  • Knowledge of Splunk SOAR (or equivalent security orchestration) and integrating Splunk with EDR, threat intel, or other security tools.
  • Experience applying Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit (MLTK) or similar for anomaly detection in operational or security data.
  • Hands-on experience with Git, CI/CD, or infrastructure-as-code practices specifically for Splunk configurations and knowledge objects.
  • Advanced Linux systems knowledge for large-scale Splunk clusters.
  • Experience supporting mission-critical, 24/7 operational environments with strict uptime and rapid incident response requirements.

Rocket EMS is seeking an experienced Manufacturing Floor Facilities Technician to support the condition, maintenance, and readiness of our production floor during the graveyard shift.

This is a hands-on position focused specifically on maintaining the manufacturing floor and production environment. The technician will perform floor maintenance, cleaning, repair, and preventative work while production activity is reduced, helping ensure the manufacturing area is clean, safe, professional, and ready for operations each morning.

This is not a janitorial position. We are looking for someone with experience maintaining flooring in an industrial or manufacturing environment who understands the equipment, chemicals, processes, and safety requirements associated with maintaining high-traffic production floors.

Responsibilities

  • Maintain manufacturing floors throughout production, warehouse, aisle, and other designated operational areas.
  • Operate industrial floor-maintenance equipment, including floor scrubbers, buffers/burnishers, polishers, and related equipment.
  • Perform routine and deep cleaning of manufacturing floors during overnight hours.
  • Strip, wax, seal, polish, or refinish flooring as appropriate for the floor type and facility requirements.
  • Remove scuffs, residue, adhesive, grease, oil, and other manufacturing-related buildup without damaging floor surfaces.
  • Perform minor floor repairs and address damaged or deteriorating areas as appropriate.
  • Maintain designated aisles, walkways, production boundaries, and other marked floor areas.
  • Support floor marking and application/removal of safety tape, aisle markings, equipment boundaries, and other visual controls.
  • Move or coordinate movement of floor-accessible items when necessary to complete scheduled maintenance.
  • Inspect flooring for cracks, trip hazards, damage, spills, or other safety concerns and report or correct issues promptly.
  • Use cleaning chemicals and floor-care products safely and according to manufacturer and facility requirements.
  • Maintain floor equipment, including routine cleaning, inspection, charging, and basic preventative maintenance.
  • Coordinate work around manufacturing schedules and equipment to minimize disruption to production.
  • Follow ESD, safety, PPE, chemical-handling, and manufacturing-floor requirements.
  • Communicate completed work and any outstanding floor or safety issues to Facilities management.

Qualifications

  • Previous industrial or manufacturing floor-care experience required.
  • Experience operating commercial/industrial auto scrubbers, buffers, burnishers, floor polishers, and similar equipment.
  • Knowledge of industrial floor-cleaning chemicals, coatings, finishes, and proper application methods.
  • Experience maintaining floors in a manufacturing, electronics, semiconductor, clean manufacturing, warehouse, or industrial environment strongly preferred.
  • Understanding of floor safety, slip prevention, chemical handling, and proper PPE.
  • Ability to work independently and manage an overnight floor-maintenance schedule.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to recognize floor damage and safety hazards.
  • Reliable attendance and ability to consistently work 8:00 PM–4:30 AM.

Preferred Experience

Experience with ESD-sensitive manufacturing environments and ESD flooring would be a big plus for Rocket. Experience maintaining epoxy, sealed concrete, resinous, or other industrial flooring is also highly desirable.

Pay Range
$25—$30 USD

ITAR/EAR Compliance: Due to the nature of the work performed at Rocket EMS, this position may require access to export-controlled technical data or technology. The successful candidate must be eligible to access such information under applicable U.S. export-control laws or be eligible for any required government authorization.

title: Senior Azure DevOps Engineer
description:
This job is with London Business School, an inclusive employer and a member of myGwork – the largest global platform for the LGBTQ+ business community. Please do not contact the recruiter directly.

Help shape how engineering teams build, deploy and operate technology at London Business School.

The Role

London Business School is looking for a Senior Azure DevOps Engineer to strengthen our engineering capability and help us mature the way we build, deploy and operate technology across a varied technology estate.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who combines deep technical expertise with ownership, judgement and the ability to influence across multiple engineering and delivery teams.

You won't simply be handed a backlog of DevOps tasks. We're looking for someone who can assess where we are today, identify the areas that will make the biggest difference, recommend practical improvements and then take those improvements through to implementation and adoption.

Working closely with engineering teams, Architecture, Cyber Security, Delivery and operational support colleagues, you will help make our technology delivery more automated, secure, reliable and predictable.

Main Responsibilities

You will take senior technical ownership across our DevOps capability, including:

  • Designing, implementing and improving Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines, reusable YAML templates and deployment controls.

  • Driving greater adoption of Infrastructure as Code, using technologies such as Terraform.

  • Improving automation across build, release, environment provisioning and operational processes.

  • Developing and evolving practical DevOps standards, patterns and reusable engineering approaches.

  • Helping teams improve release quality, deployment reliability, rollback capability and operational readiness.

  • Strengthening monitoring, logging, alerting and observability across applications and platforms.

  • Embedding security into pipelines and cloud infrastructure, including secrets management, identity controls and automated security checks.

  • Identifying technical debt, manual processes and recurring operational issues and turning them into prioritised improvement opportunities.

  • Working across multiple teams to resolve dependencies and differing levels of DevOps maturity.

  • Coaching and enabling engineers so that good DevOps practice becomes embedded across our teams rather than dependent on one individual.

  • Translating agreed engineering priorities into a pragmatic, phased DevOps improvement roadmap and driving delivery against it.

Who We Are Looking For

You'll be an experienced DevOps or cloud engineer who is comfortable operating with a high degree of independence.

Alongside strong hands-on Azure expertise, you'll be able to demonstrate:

  • Strong experience with Azure and Azure DevOps.

  • Deep understanding of CI/CD and experience designing scalable deployment pipelines.

  • Strong practical experience with Infrastructure as Code, particularly Terraform.

  • Experience implementing effective monitoring, logging and alerting.

  • Good understanding of Git, branching strategies and modern release and deployment approaches.

  • Experience embedding security and governance into cloud and pipeline configurations.

  • The ability to take ambiguous technical problems from discovery through recommendation, implementation and adoption.

  • Strong judgement when balancing delivery priorities, operational risk and longer-term engineering improvement.

  • The confidence to challenge existing approaches constructively and recommend better alternatives.

  • Experience influencing engineering standards and securing adoption across multiple teams.

  • A collaborative approach and the ability to coach and enable other engineers.

  • Azure DevOps Engineer Expert certification, or equivalent demonstrable experience, would be highly valued.

Benefits You Can Enjoy

  • Generous annual leave of 27 days plus extra days between Christmas and New Year

  • USS pension, 14.5% employer contribution (in return for employee enrolment and contribution)

  • Free onsite gym and swimming pool

  • Amazing range of professional development to support your career path

  • Wellbeing offering to support your physical, mental and financial health

At London Business School, we support Smart Working - a hybrid approach designed to help you achieve a healthy work-life balance while delivering the best outcomes for your role and the needs of our customers. All roles require a minimum of two days on campus each week to foster a vibrant, collaborative community.


For this role specifically, you will be expected to be on campus 3 days per week.

We operate with 'core hours' - 10:00-15:00 - to maximise opportunities for connection and collaboration across teams during the working day. Outside of these hours, you may still be required for meetings or collaboration based on your role and customer needs. Additionally, we offer Protected Time - a flexible, one-hour slot, within the working week dedicated to your learning and development, wellbeing, or focused, quiet work

Why London Business School?

London Business School; a global and vibrant business community based in three of the world's most dynamic cities, London, Dubai and Riyadh. It's where extraordinary minds and diverse perspectives connect, to have a profound impact on the way the world does business and the way business impacts the world. We offer best in class hybrid learning to our students and participants, whilst creating a flexible, supportive and dynamic working environment for our people to excel in, whatever their location.

Our commitment to driving inclusion and belonging

We are a globally reaching institution, committed to creating tangible and sustainable change in driving inclusion & belonging within our School, education and society at large. We are dedicated to creating an environment where everyone in our community feels they belong and thrive. This is a key school priority, and we want everyone who joins LBS to feel respected, welcomed, and heard.

title: Supervisor, Global Technology Audit
description:
Summary

The Supervisor, Global Technology Audit serves as the Internal Audit subject matter expert for cybersecurity risk, security architecture, threat management, and technical security controls.

The incumbent is responsible for executing complex technology audit work with a high degree of technical independence and expert-level domain judgement. This role leads defined audit components as Functional Coordinator (FC) and may serve as Overall Coordinator (OC) for less complex engagements, applying threat-informed, risk-based thinking to assess control design and operating effectiveness across cybersecurity, infrastructure, cloud, identity, and emerging technology domains. The Supervisor functions as the technical subject matter resource on assigned engagements capable of independently evaluating security architecture and interpreting technical artifacts. This role coaches Senior Auditors on technical rigor and professional skepticism, and contributes to audit methodology development, technical testing procedure design, and continuous improvement of audit quality.

Candidates are expected to develop and sustain deep practitioner-level expertise in one or more high-risk technology domains, providing technical continuity, audit program ownership, and domain leadership over a longer tenure in the function. The incumbent partners with Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, Cloud Engineering, Digital Technology, Compliance, and Business stakeholders to assess cybersecurity risks, evaluate control effectiveness, and provide independent assurance over the organization's security posture.

Responsibilities

Audit Leadership:

  • Lead end-to-end execution of complex technology audit engagements as Functional Coordinator (FC), with full accountability for scoping, fieldwork, evidence assessment, and findings development in cybersecurity, infrastructure, cloud, and IT general controls domains.
  • Serve as the technical subject matter resource for assigned anchor domains, independently evaluating control design and operating effectiveness in areas including cloud security architecture, identity and access management, vulnerability and patch management, network security, endpoint detection and response, and privileged access governance.

Cybersecurity Assessments:

  • Lead complex cybersecurity audits, assessments, and advisory reviews across enterprise technology environments.
  • Develop risk assessments, audit programs, testing strategies, and report deliverables for cybersecurity-related engagements.
  • Independently evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of technical, administrative, and detective security controls.
  • Identify emerging cyber risks, control deficiencies, and opportunities to strengthen the organization's control environment.

Technical Security Assessments:

  • Review and assess:
    • Security architecture and infrastructure controls
    • Identity and Access Management (IAM)
    • Privileged Access Management (PAM)
    • Cloud security configurations and governance
    • Network security and segmentation
    • Endpoint protection controls
    • Vulnerability management programs
    • Security monitoring and threat detection capabilities
    • Incident response and cyber resilience processes
  • Assess technical evidence including architecture diagrams, firewall rules, IAM configurations, SIEM detections, vulnerability scan results, cloud security configurations, and security control implementations.

Threat-Informed Assurance:

  • Utilize MITRE ATT&CK and industry frameworks to evaluate preventive and detective control coverage against relevant threat tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
  • Assess the effectiveness of security controls against the enterprise threat landscape and risk profile.
  • Evaluate detection, response, and recovery capabilities across key cyber threat scenarios.

Governance & Risk Management:

  • Evaluate cybersecurity governance frameworks, policies, standards, and oversight mechanisms.
  • Assess enterprise cybersecurity risk management and third-party cybersecurity risk practices.
  • Evaluate alignment with industry frameworks and regulatory requirements.

Advisory & Strategic Support:

  • Provide cybersecurity expertise during technology transformation, cloud adoption, and emerging technology initiatives.
  • Monitor evolving cyber threats, attack techniques, regulatory developments, and industry best practices.
  • Support development of Internal Audit methodologies related to cybersecurity assurance and technical risk assessments.

Stakeholder Engagement & Leadership:

  • Present audit results, risk themes, and recommendations to management and senior leadership.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor while maintaining Internal Audit independence.
  • Mentor audit staff and contribute to development of technical cybersecurity audit capabilities across the Internal Audit function.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Information Security, or related field from an accredited university.
  • 5+ years of experience in cybersecurity audits, technology risk, IT audit, or cloud audit.
  • CISSP, CISM, or CISA
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical risks into business-focused recommendations.
  • Experience presenting findings and recommendations to senior management.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, or CRISC with demonstrated technical specialization
  • Strong understanding of:
    • Security architecture and engineering
    • Network security
    • Cloud security
    • Identity and Access Management
    • Security monitoring and incident response
    • Vulnerability management
  • Ability to independently analyze technical security artifacts and determine control design and operating effectiveness without reliance on auditee interpretation.
  • Working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK and threat-informed control assessments.
  • Experience leading audits, risk assessments, or technical security reviews involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Experience auditing cloud environments including Azure, AWS, or GCP.
  • Experience assessing security operations, threat detection, incident response, or cyber resilience programs.
  • Knowledge of NIST CSF, NIST 800-series publications, CIS Controls, ISO 27001, and other cybersecurity frameworks.
  • Experience supporting or leading assessments involving AI, cloud, third-party risk management, or emerging technology risks.

title: Emergency Medical Technician Basic-Emergency Transport
description:
Overview

EMT/AEMT/Paramedic (Ground Ambulance)

UnityPoint Health - Allen

Shift: FTE : .01; As Needed- PRN

As a member of our interdisciplinary team, the EMS professional provides expert prehospital care to patients and their families. This role requires strong patient‑service skills, the ability to perform effectively under pressure, and sound clinical judgment when making rapid decisions regarding patient health. The EMS professional delivers care within the State of Iowa Scope of Practice, consistent with their state certification level and in alignment with hospital policies and procedures.

Why UnityPoint Health?

At UnityPoint Health, you matter. We’re proud to be recognized as a Top 150 Place to Work in Healthcare by Becker's Healthcare several years in a row for our commitment to our team members.

Our competitive Total Rewards program offers benefits options that align with your needs and priorities, no matter what life stage you’re in. Here are just a few:

  • Expect paid time off, parental leave, 401K matching and an employee recognition program.
  • Dental and health insurance, paid holidays, short and long-term disability and more. We even offer pet insurance for your four-legged family members.
  • Early access to earned wages with Daily Pay, tuition reimbursement to help further your career and adoption assistance to help you grow your family.

With a collective goal to champion a culture of belonging where everyone feels valued and respected, we honor the ways people are unique and embrace what brings us together.

And, we believe equipping you with support and development opportunities is a vital part of delivering an exceptional employment experience.

Find a fulfilling career and make a difference with UnityPoint Health.

Responsibilities

  • Assesses the needs of patients and families through the interpretation of written medical director protocols and creating an appropriate patient care plan within their scope of practice.
  • Adapts and adjusts the patient’s care plan according to the patient’s needs in the prehospital setting and may serve as primary attendant of patient while on scene and/or during transportation.
  • Prepared to physically intervene in potentially violent situations to provide patient care in accordance to departmental policies and procedures.
  • Promptly completes documentation to assure an accurate legal record of patient’s care.
  • Carries out high quality patient care while following the scope of practice set out by the State of Iowa Public Health Department Bureau of EMS and this ambulance service.
  • Ability to transport a patient or community member, in a safe manner through the utilization of an ambulance or secure car, potentially during adverse weather conditions.

Education:

  • High school graduate or equivalent
  • Successful completion of EMS training from an approved training course

Licensure/Certification:

  • Current Iowa certification as an EMT, Iowa Advanced-EMT, or EMT-PM level required
  • Valid Iowa driver’s license for at least three years with an acceptable or clear rating according to the Motor Vehicle Record chart. (see below).
  • Must have a minimum of two years driving experience with no record of DUI, DWI, or similar alcohol or drug related offenses over the past five years.
  • No record of reckless driving, careless driving, speeding over 15 miles above the speed limit, fleeing or eluding a police officer, chemical test refusal, leaving the scene of an accident, driving after revocation or suspension, or passing a stopped school bus in the last five years.

Experience:

  • Previous EMS experience preferred

title: Advanced Software Engineer
description:
As an Advanced Software Engineer here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will be responsible for a variety of professional-level engineering responsibilities and requires the application of advanced knowledge of software engineering disciplines, processes, and tools to execute project subtasks and ensure compliance with technical, quality, and customer requirements. You will contribute to the design, development, integration, verification, and release of software features for Avionics Displays systems, algorithms, and software frameworks. This position plays an important role in delivering products that meet customer specifications, certification requirements, and organizational quality standards. The role also involves regular interaction with internal stakeholders and external customers to support project execution and product compliance.

This Advanced Software Engineer is recognized as an emerging authority within Integrated Flight Deck Systems COE and is expected to help define and improve engineering processes, recommend enhancements to technical methods, and mentor early-career engineers. The ideal candidate demonstrates strong technical depth, independent problem-solving ability, and the capability to lead feature decomposition, coordinate development activities, and support programs execution. You will directly impact product delivery by executing engineering subtasks, identifying technical improvements, driving feature implementation, and supporting the successful completion of customer-driven software solutions.

You will report directly to our Sr Software Engineering Manager and you’ll work out of our Phoenix, AZ location on a hybrid work schedule. Note: For the first 90 days, New Hires must be prepared to work 100% onsite M-F.

We are seeking a Guest Service Agent to serve as the welcoming face and problem-solving heart of our front desk. In this role, you are responsible for the guest’s check-in and check-out experience, reservations support, and being the go-to resource for everything a guest needs during their stay; from restaurant recommendations to resolving the occasional hiccup with grace.

The ideal Guest Service Agent is a natural people-person who genuinely enjoys making someone's day better, whether that's a road-weary traveler checking in at midnight or a regular who just wants their usual room. They're quick on their feet with our property management system, comfortable juggling phones, walk-ups, and special requests all at once, and calm under pressure when things don't go exactly to plan. Equal parts concierge, problem-solver, and brand ambassador, they take genuine pride in being the first and last impression of a guest's stay, and they bring that same warmth to every teammate they work alongside.

Key Responsibilities

· Warmly welcome guests at check-in and check-out, setting the tone for a memorable stay from the first hello

· Operate the property management system (PMS) to process reservations, check-ins/outs, room assignments, and payments accurately

· Handle cash, credit transactions, and folio adjustments with precision and full accountability

title: Business Controller (m/f/d)
description:
As a Business Controller, you will be responsible for monitoring and analysing business performance, supporting budgeting and forecasting activities, and providing financial insights to local leadership and senior management.

You will work closely with different business functions to ensure accurate financial reporting, identify performance gaps, and drive corrective actions and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Review monthly P&L results and key performance indicators, identifying variances, errors and improvement opportunities.
  • Analyse actual results against budget and forecast, develop corrective action plans and monitor their implementation.
  • Prepare and coordinate monthly performance reviews and management reporting.
  • Monitor working capital indicators, including DSO, DPO and DIO, against defined targets.
  • Support the preparation of the annual budget and forecasts, covering P&L, CAPEX, working capital and operating expenses.
  • Develop financial business scenarios and forecasts in response to significant business changes.
  • Prepare cash flow forecasts and support funding requests when required.
  • Define and maintain cost allocation rules, accounting principles and business structures.
  • Monitor overhead and operational cost centres and ensure accurate cost reporting.
  • Work closely with business teams to understand operational KPIs and assess their impact on financial performance.
  • Support invoicing and internal cost recharge processes.
  • Participate in procurement approval workflows and provide financial input where required.
  • Support statutory and group audits.
  • Monitor outstanding receivables, doubtful debts, and related collection processes.
  • Manage local insurance requirements and monitor related processes and payments.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in Controlling or Business Controlling.
  • Solid background in Finance and Accounting.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to understand complex business situations.
  • Good understanding of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting and business performance analysis.
  • Strong systems-thinking and data analysis skills.
  • Confident command of English, both written and spoken.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with different business functions and senior stakeholders.
  • Strategic mindset combined with a hands-on, solution-oriented and execution-focused approach.
  • Proactive attitude towards continuous improvement and process optimisation.
  • This role offers the opportunity to work closely with local leadership and multiple business functions, providing financial insights that support business decision-making.
  • The position combines financial analysis, business partnering, planning and performance management, with a strong focus on continuous improvement.
  • Experience with TM1, Coupa or similar financial/procurement systems will be considered an advantage.
  • The successful candidate should be comfortable working in a dynamic, international environment and managing multiple priorities.
